pages.title: App and running
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.App: the application class, run, screenshot, post, load_font and the window options of a Python desktop app.
pages.intro:
Everything you need to start an application. See also the
            [architecture](/pyzed/guides/architecture/) guide.
        

See also [multiple windows](/pyzed/guides/windows/) and [async and subscriptions](/pyzed/guides/async/).

pyzed.App.desc:
Base class for applications (Elm architecture, like Iced). It is also the **main
window**, so it inherits everything from [`Window`](#window). Override `view()` and, if you use
messages, `update(message)`. State lives in instance attributes.

| Class attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `"Pyzed"` | Window title. Can be a callable (or property) that returns the text. |
| `size` | `(1280, 800)` | Initial window size. |
| `font_size` | `14` | Default text size. |
| `theme` | `themes.PYZED_DARK` | A `Theme`, the name of a registered theme or `themes.auto(light, dark)`. Change it at any time. |
| `style` | `None` | The global style: a `pz.Style` for the whole window. Its text color, size, background, border color and radius become theme tokens. See [Styles](/pyzed/theming/styles/#the-global-style). |
| `system_dark` | `True` | Whether the system is in dark mode (updated by the runtime). |
| `tab_focus` | `True` | Tab and Shift+Tab move the focus between the fields of the window. See [Accessibility](/pyzed/guides/accessibility/). |
| `arrow_focus` | `False` | The arrow keys no control used move the focus to the nearest control that way (remotes, rotary knobs). |
| `device` | `None` | The device profile: a name (`"touch"`, `"automotive"`, `"mobile"`, `"kiosk"`, `"tv"`) or a `pz.Device`. See [Devices](/pyzed/guides/devices/). |
| `splash` | `None` | A [`Splash`](#splash) window shown before the main window opens. |
| `rendering` | `None` | A [`Rendering`](#rendering): GPU or CPU, graphics API, GPU and vsync. `None` reads `[tool.pyzed.rendering]` of the project's `pyproject.toml`. |

The remaining window options (`min_size`, `resizable`, `decorations`, `icon`, `scale`…) are on `Window`.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `view()` | Returns the widget tree. Called after every message. |
| `update(message)` | Receives messages. Can return a `Command`, a list of them, a coroutine, a generator (regular or async) or another message. |
| `on_start()` | Optional. Runs once at startup; can return a `Command` or a coroutine. |
| `on_key(combo)` | Optional. Receives every key as `"ctrl-shift-p"`, `"escape"`, `"up"`… |
| `on_key_up(key)` | Optional. Receives key releases by name (`"left"`, `"space"`). |
| `subscriptions()` | Optional. Returns the active subscriptions (`pz.every`, `pz.listen`). Re-evaluated after every `update`. |
| `resolved_theme()` | The concrete `Theme` in use (resolves names and `themes.auto`). |
| `run()` | Opens the window and blocks until the app exits. |
| `screenshot(path, *, size=None, scale=2.0, wait=0.1)` | Renders the current state to a PNG without a window. |

If `view()` raises an exception, the window shows the traceback instead of closing.

pyzed.run.desc: Runs an app: opens the window and blocks until it is closed. Accepts the class or an instance.

params.reload: Hot reload: saving a project file updates the running window and keeps its state. `None` follows `PYZED_RELOAD` (set by `pyzed dev`).
params.watch: Extra folders or files to watch for hot reload.

pyzed.screenshot.desc: Renders `app` offscreen (no window, no GPU) and saves a PNG. Useful for tests and documentation.

params.wait: Seconds to wait before capturing (for `on_start` tasks).

pyzed.post.desc: Sends a message to the running app from **any thread**. Raises `RuntimeError` if no app is running.

pyzed.UNCHANGED.desc: Return it from a callback that changed nothing on screen (a pointer move you only record, a focus change): the window is not rebuilt. Any other return value redraws as usual. See the [performance guide](/pyzed/guides/performance/).

pyzed.load_font.desc: Loads an extra font (path to a `.ttf`/`.otf` or its bytes) so you can use it by family name: `text("hello", font="JetBrains Mono")`.

params.source: Path to the font file, or `bytes`.

pyzed.Window.desc:
An extra window with its own `view()`, title, size and theme. Open it by returning
`window.open()` (or `Command.open_window(window)`). Inside it, `self.app` is the app, so
windows share state; the messages it produces go to its `update()`, which by default
forwards them to `app.update()`.

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `"Pyzed"` | Text or callable. |
| `size` | `(800, 600)` | Initial size. |
| `min_size`, `max_size` | `None` | Size limits. |
| `position` | `None` | `"center"` or `(x, y)`. |
| `resizable` | `True` | Whether it can be resized. |
| `decorations` | `True` | `False` removes the system frame (custom title bar with `drag()`). |
| `transparent`, `maximized`, `fullscreen` | `False` | Initial state. `fullscreen = "exclusive"` takes the screen over with its own video mode (Windows, X11, macOS). |
| `monitor` | `None` | The screen it opens on: an index of `pz.monitors()`. |
| `always_on_top`, `always_on_bottom` | `False` | `True` keeps it above (or below) the other windows. |
| `closable`, `minimizable` | `True` | `False` removes those buttons. |
| `skip_taskbar` | `False` | Leaves it out of the taskbar (Windows). |
| `hide_cursor` | `False` | Hides the pointer over it (touch panels). |
| `kiosk` | `False` | Fullscreen, no frame or buttons, above the rest, and the user cannot close it. See [Screens and kiosks](/pyzed/guides/windows/#screens-and-kiosks). |
| `design_size`, `stretch` | `None`, `"expand"` | Lays the view out for `design_size` and scales it to the window: `"expand"` grows into the space left, `"fit"` keeps the design centered. See [Design resolution](/pyzed/guides/devices/#design-resolution). |
| `scale` | `1.0` | UI scale. |
| `theme` | `None` | Its own theme; `None` uses the app's. |
| `style` | `None` | Its own global style; `None` uses the app's. |
| `icon` | `None` | The window's icon (title bar, taskbar): a path to an image or its bytes. Set it on `pz.Window` to give every window the same one. See [Icons and metadata](/pyzed/packaging/icons-metadata/#the-window-icon). |
| `app_id` | `None` | Linux: the app id the desktop matches with a `.desktop` file (`com.acme.shop`). |
| `app` | — | The app that owns the window (assigned when it opens). |
| `window_size` | — | Current size in logical pixels (updated by the runtime). |
| `window_position` | — | Where the window is on the screen, its outer top-left corner (updated by the runtime; `None` on Wayland). |
| `isolated` | `False` | `True` promises that only its own messages change what it shows: messages from other windows and the app's timers skip its `view()`, layout and redraw. See [Many windows](/pyzed/guides/performance/#many-windows). |

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `view()` | Required. Returns the window's widget tree. |
| `update(message)` | Receives the window's messages (by default forwards them to the app). |
| `open()` / `close()` / `drag()` | Commands to open it, close it or start moving it. |
| `is_open` | Whether it is open. |
| `resolved_theme()` | The concrete `Theme` it uses. |
| `on_open()` | When it opens. |
| `on_close()` | When the user asks to close it; return `False` to prevent it. |
| `on_resize(width, height)` | When it is resized. |
| `on_key(combo)`, `subscriptions()` | As in `App`. |
| `refresh()` | Draws an `isolated` window again on the next update (safe from any thread). |
| `set_fullscreen(fullscreen=True, monitor=None, exclusive=False)`, `set_window_level(level)` | Commands for fullscreen (on a screen, maybe exclusive) and for staying above or below the others. |
| `on_file_hover(path)`, `on_file_drop(path)`, `on_file_leave()` | Files dragged from the system over the window, dropped on it (once per file) or taken away. By default they go to the `ui.DropZone` they land on. |

pyzed.Splash.desc: A splash screen: a frameless window with an image, centered on the screen, shown while the app starts. Give it to `App.splash`; it stays up for `duration` seconds at least, then the main window opens and the splash closes. See [Splash screen](/pyzed/packaging/build/#splash-screen).

params.image: Path to the picture (PNG, JPEG...) or its bytes.
params.duration: Seconds it stays up, at least.
params.size: Window size; default: the image's, scaled down to fit 900 × 600.
params.text: Text written over the bottom of the image (for example `"Loading…"`).
params.background: Color behind the image (for pictures with transparency).
params.title: Window title (the taskbar shows it).

pyzed.Splash.example:
class Shop(pz.App):
    splash = pz.Splash("assets/splash.png", duration=1.5, text="Loading…")

pyzed.Rendering.desc: How the app draws its windows: on the GPU or the CPU, which graphics API and GPU, vsync, antialiasing and frame rate limits. Each field is `"auto"` by default (Pyzed decides). Give it to `App.rendering`, or set the same keys in `[tool.pyzed.rendering]` of the project's `pyproject.toml`, which `pz.run`, the designer and `pyzed build` read. See [Rendering](/pyzed/editor/settings/#rendering).

params.renderer: `"auto"`, `"gpu"` (needed by shaders) or `"cpu"` (tiny-skia: starts faster, less memory, works everywhere).
params.power: `"auto"`, `"high"` (the dedicated GPU) or `"low"` (the integrated one, saves battery).
params.vsync: `"auto"`, `"on"` (no tearing) or `"off"` (draws as fast as it can).
params.present: How frames reach the screen, winning over `vsync`: `"auto"`, `"fifo"` (least power), `"fifo_relaxed"`, `"mailbox"` (low latency without tearing) or `"immediate"` (lowest latency, may tear).
params.antialiasing: Edges of canvas drawings, charts and curves: `"auto"` (4x), `"off"`, `"2x"`, `"4x"`, `"8x"` or `"16x"`.
params.frame_latency: Frames the GPU may prepare ahead: `"auto"` (1, answers input soonest), `"1"`, `"2"` or `"3"`.
params.memory: `"auto"` (low), `"low"` or `"performance"`: how the GPU renderer allocates memory.
params.gpu: Part of the name of the GPU to use (`"nvidia"`, `"intel"`); `""` lets `power` decide.
params.max_fps: The most frames per second animations draw (`0` follows the screen). Input and new content are drawn at once.
params.background_fps: The same for windows without the focus: `0` pauses their animations, `None` uses `max_fps`.

pyzed.safe_area.desc: The parts of the screen the system draws over, in logical pixels: `(top, right, bottom, left)`. On Android: the status and navigation bars, the camera cutout and the soft keyboard while it is open; zeros on a desktop. Windows keep clear of them unless `safe_area = False`.

pyzed.monitors.desc: The connected screens as a list of `pz.Monitor`: `index`, `name`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` (logical pixels on the desktop), `scale`, `refresh_rate` in hertz and `primary`. Read when a window opens (empty before the first one) and by `Command.list_monitors`.

pyzed.Monitor.desc: A screen from `pz.monitors()`. `size` and `position` give `(width, height)` and `(x, y)`.

pyzed.Device.desc: A device profile: how the device is used (touch, pointer, arrow keys) and drawn on (scale, design size, quality). Pyzed fills in the window and rendering options the app leaves at their defaults. See [Devices](/pyzed/guides/devices/).

params.name: Its name, for `pz.media("device: ...")`.
params.touch: Touched more than clicked: `pz.media("pointer: coarse")` is true.
params.pointer: `False` hides the pointer over the windows.
params.kiosk: The main window opens as a kiosk.
params.arrow_focus: The arrow keys move the focus.
params.scale: Interface scale of the windows that leave `scale` at 1.
params.min_target: The smallest comfortable control in logical pixels.
params.design_size: The window size the app was designed for.
params.reduced_motion: `True` turns animations off, `None` follows the system.
params.rendering: `pz.Rendering` fields on top of the quality level.

pyzed.Device.example:
class Panel(pz.App):
    device = pz.Device("panel", touch=True, kiosk=True, quality="low")

pyzed.device.desc: The device profile the app runs with (`desktop` before `pz.run` picks one).

pyzed.set_device.desc: Uses a profile from now on (a name or a `pz.Device`; `None` picks one again as `pz.run` does) and returns it.

pyzed.background.desc: Makes a function return a command that runs it off the UI thread: on a worker thread (an `async def` on Pyzed's asyncio loop) or, with `process=True`, in another process. The result reaches `then` on the UI thread. See [Off the UI thread](/pyzed/guides/async/#off-the-ui-thread-pzbackground).

params.then: A callable, or the name of a method of the same object, that gets the result (each value of a generator); without it the result goes to `update`.
params.latest: `True` delivers only the newest call's result (searches as you type).
params.process: `True` runs it in a worker process, for CPU-heavy pure Python: a function at the top of a module, with picklable arguments and result.

pyzed.renderer_info.desc: The GPU and the graphics API drawing the windows, like `("NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060", "Vulkan")`, or `("CPU", "tiny-skia")` with the CPU renderer; `None` until the first window is open.

pyzed.every.desc: A subscription that sends `message` to `update` every `seconds` seconds (like Iced's `time::every`). If `message` is a callable, it is called. Return it from `subscriptions()`.
pyzed.every.example:
def subscriptions(self):
    return [pz.every(1, "tick")] if self.running else []

pyzed.listen.desc: A subscription that runs `function()` (a generator or async generator) while it is active and sends every value it yields to `update`. Ideal for websockets and streams.
pyzed.listen.example:
async def feed():
    async for message in websocket:
        yield message

def subscriptions(self):
    return [pz.listen(feed)]

pyzed.frames.desc: A subscription that calls `callback(dt)` once per displayed frame (in sync with the screen, usually 60 times a second), with `dt` the seconds since the previous frame (at most 0.25). Made for games and simulations: move things by `speed * dt`. See [Making games](/pyzed/games/).

params.max_fps: Highest rate where the display does not wait for vsync (software rendering). Default 240.

pyzed.pressed.desc: The keys held down right now, as a `frozenset` of names without modifiers (`"left"`, `"space"`, `"a"`…). Empty when no window is open. Poll it every frame for continuous movement; `on_key` is for one-off presses.

pyzed.is_pressed.desc: Whether any of `keys` is held down. `held` replaces `pressed()` (handy in tests).

params.held: Optional set of keys to use instead of `pressed()`.

pyzed.Subscription.desc: What `every` and `listen` return. It is identified by its `key`: as long as `subscriptions()` keeps returning one with the same key, it keeps running; when it disappears, it stops.

pyzed.spawn.desc: Schedules a coroutine on Pyzed's asyncio loop without waiting for its result and returns a `concurrent.futures.Future`. To receive the result in the UI, return the coroutine from `update` or use `Command.perform`.

pyzed.asyncio_loop.desc: The asyncio loop (on a background thread) where Pyzed runs every coroutine. It starts the first time it is used.

pyzed.on.desc: Attaches common event handlers to a widget; same as `widget.on(...)`. Events: `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `mouse_down`, `mouse_up`, `mouse_enter`, `mouse_leave`, `mouse_move`, `scroll`, `drag_start`, `drag`, `drag_end`, `focus`, `blur`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `resize`. See [Events](/pyzed/guides/events/).

params.widget: The widget (a string is wrapped in a container).
params.cursor: Mouse cursor over the widget, such as `"pointer"` or `"grab"`.
params.handlers: `event=handler` pairs. A handler that takes an argument gets a `pz.Event`; a non-callable value is a message for `update`; `None` removes it.

pyzed.on.example: pz.container(card, padding=12).on(click=self.select, drag=lambda e: self.move(e.dx, e.dy))

pyzed.Event.desc: What happened, passed to event handlers: `type`, `x`, `y` (relative to the widget), `dx`, `dy` (scroll or drag movement), `width`, `height`, `button`, `key`, `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `logo`, `window_x`, `window_y`, `screen_x`, `screen_y` (the pointer in the window and on the screen), and `value`/`source` for custom events.

params.x: Pointer x, relative to the widget.
params.y: Pointer y, relative to the widget.
params.window_x: Pointer x in the window (outside it when a drag is released outside).
params.screen_x: Pointer x on the screen, or `None` where the platform does not say where windows are (Wayland). `event.screen` gives `(screen_x, screen_y)`.
params.screen_y: Pointer y on the screen, or `None`.
params.screen: `(screen_x, screen_y)`, or `None` when the platform does not report window positions.

pyzed.Dock.desc: An editor-style workspace: a `center` with `pz.DockPanel`s docked left, right, bottom or top. Users resize a side by dragging its inner edge and move a panel by dragging its tab onto a drop zone (or from the tab's right-click menu). `on_layout` receives the layout as a dict to save; pass it back as `layout=`. See [Layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/#docks-and-resizable-panels).

params.kwargs: Props and handlers by name, plus `key=`.
params.on_layout: Called with `event.value` = `{positions, sizes, active, hidden}` when panels move, resize or switch.

pyzed.Dock.example:
pz.Dock(center=editor, panels=[
    pz.DockPanel("project", "Project", tree, icon="folder", side="left"),
    pz.DockPanel("terminal", "Terminal", terminal, icon="terminal", side="bottom"),
], layout=self.layout, on_layout=lambda e: setattr(self, "layout", e.value))

params.id: Stable id (used in the saved layout).
params.title: Tab title.

pyzed.Component.desc: Base class for custom components, like React components: annotated class attributes are props, other attributes are state kept between renders, `render()` returns widgets and `events` declares custom events raised with `self.emit(name, value)`. Calling the class returns a widget. Components appear in the designer's toolbox. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/).

params.args: Props, in declaration order (or the children, when the class has a `children` prop).
params.kwargs: Props by name, `on_<event>=` handlers (custom, lifecycle or common events), `key=` to keep state when items move, and `style=`, `class_=`, `id=` and `animate=`.

pyzed.Color.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a color (a theme token or `"#rrggbb"`): the designer shows a color picker for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Icon.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a Lucide icon name: the designer shows an icon picker for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Multiline.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds long text: the designer shows a text area for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.FilePath.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a file path: the designer shows the path with a button that opens the system's file dialog (a `pathlib.Path` annotation does the same). A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.FolderPath.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a folder: the designer shows the path with a button that opens the system's folder dialog. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Range.desc: Limits of a number prop, used with `typing.Annotated`: the designer shows a number box limited to them. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/#in-the-designer).

pyzed.provide.desc: A context manager that shares values with every component rendered inside, like React's context. Read them with `pz.use_context(name)` or `self.context(name)`. A component's `provide()` method does the same for what it renders. See [Children, context and styles](/pyzed/guides/components/#children-context-and-styles).

pyzed.use_context.desc: The closest value shared as `name` with `pz.provide` or a component's `provide()`.

pyzed.state.desc: Declares a private state variable on a component class: the parent cannot pass it, and every instance starts with its own copy of the default (lists and dicts are safe). The designer lists it next to the props. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/).

params.default: Initial value, copied for each instance.

pyzed.component.LIFECYCLE_EVENTS.desc: Names of the lifecycle events every component raises (`mount`, `unmount`...).

pyzed.events.CATALOG.desc: Every event name Pyzed knows, mapped to its `EventInfo` (what raises it and what `event.value` holds).

pyzed.events.COMMON.desc: The events every widget accepts through `widget.on(...)` (click, hover, focus, keys...).

pyzed.t.desc: The text for `key` in the current language, formatted with `values`. Falls back from `"es_AR"` to `"es"`, then to the fallback language, then to the key. See [Languages](/pyzed/guides/i18n/).

params.language: Look it up in another language.
params.default: Returned when the key is missing (default: the key).
params.values: Values for `{name}` placeholders; `count=` also picks the plural form.

pyzed.t.example:
i18n.add("es", {"greeting": "¡Hola, {name}!", "files": {"one": "{count} archivo", "other": "{count} archivos"}})
i18n.set_language("es")
pz.t("greeting", name="Kev"), pz.t("files", count=3)

pyzed.i18n.add.desc: Adds or overrides texts for a language. Nested tables become dotted keys; `{"one": ..., "other": ...}` tables are plural forms.

pyzed.i18n.load.desc: Loads every `<language>.json` and `<language>.toml` in `folder`; returns the languages found.

pyzed.i18n.set_language.desc: Switches the language. The app shows it on its next render, so call it from a handler.

pyzed.i18n.set_fallback.desc: The language used when a text is missing (default `"en"`).

pyzed.i18n.on_change.desc: Calls `listener(language)` after every switch; returns a function that removes it.

params.listener: Callable that receives the new language.

pyzed.i18n.system_language.desc: The operating system's language (`LANG`, `LC_ALL` or the locale).

params.default: Returned when the system reports none.

pyzed.i18n.has.desc: Whether `key` has a text in the language or its fallbacks.

params.language: Language to check (default: the current one).

pyzed.validation_errors.desc: Turns a validation error into `{field: message}`, ready for `ui.field(..., error=)`. Accepts a Pydantic or SQLModel `ValidationError`, a Django `ValidationError`, the JSON of a FastAPI 422 response (`{"detail": [...]}`) or its `detail` list. Nested fields are joined with dots and errors that belong to no field use the key `""`. Only the first message of each field is kept. See [Integrations](/pyzed/integrations/overview/#validation-errors-on-each-field).

params.error: The error, or the JSON of the response.

pages.title: Command
pages.description: API reference for Pyzed commands: the side effects returned by update and callbacks, such as focusing fields, closing and background tasks.

pyzed.Command.desc: The command class. Don't instantiate it directly: use its static methods.

params.id: The `id` you passed to the widget.

pyzed.Command.focus_next.desc: Moves the keyboard focus to the next field of the window, wrapping around (what Tab does).

pyzed.Command.focus_previous.desc: Moves the keyboard focus to the previous field of the window (what Shift+Tab does).

pyzed.Command.focus_direction.desc: Moves the keyboard focus to the nearest field that way on the screen (TV remotes, rotary knobs). `App.arrow_focus` does it with the arrow keys. See [Devices](/pyzed/guides/devices/#focus-with-the-arrow-keys).

pyzed.Command.select_all.desc: Focuses the `text_input` with that `id` and selects all its text (typing replaces it).

pyzed.Command.set_editor_text.desc: Replaces the content of the `code_editor` with that `id`. Editors are uncontrolled: `text` is only the initial value.

pyzed.Command.set_editor_cursor.desc: Moves the editor cursor (line and column start at 1). Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.fold_all.desc: Folds every block of the editor (`fold=False` unfolds them all). Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.fold_line.desc: Folds (or unfolds) the block that starts at `line`, by indentation. Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.editor_action.desc: Runs a named editor action in the editor with that `id`, as if its key was pressed: Zed's action name in snake case (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`, `"move_line_up"`, `"toggle_comments"`…). Raises `ValueError` for an unknown name.

params.name: The action's name (`Command.editor_actions()` lists them; `"editor::SelectNext"` works too).

pyzed.Command.select_editor_ranges.desc: Selects ranges of the editor, one cursor each; the first one is the primary cursor. Unfolds what hides them and works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

params.ranges: `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends (an empty range is a plain cursor).

pyzed.Command.replace_editor_ranges.desc: Replaces ranges of the editor with texts as one undo step, and calls the editor's `on_change` (search and replace).

params.edits: `[((line, column, end_line, end_column), text)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.

pyzed.Command.scroll_to_end.desc: Scrolls the `scrollable` with that `id` to the end.

pyzed.Command.message.desc: Sends `message` to `update` again on the next cycle.

pyzed.Command.perform.desc: Runs `function()` in the background and delivers the result to `then(result)` on the UI thread. `function` can be regular (runs on a thread) or `async def` (runs on Pyzed's asyncio loop). If it returns a generator (regular or async), `then` is called with each value. It also accepts an already created coroutine or generator (`fetch(url)` instead of `fetch`). Without `then`, results go to `update`. If `function` raises, the error is printed.

params.function: Function with no arguments that does the slow work.
params.then: Callable that receives the result (or `None` to send it to `update`).

pyzed.Command.scroll_to.desc: Scrolls the `scrollable` with that `id` to an absolute position in pixels.

pyzed.Command.paste.desc: Reads the clipboard and calls `then(text)` (empty string if it is empty).

pyzed.Command.paste_image.desc: Reads an image from the clipboard (a screenshot, a copied picture) and calls `then(png)` with its PNG bytes, or `then(None)` when the clipboard holds no image.

params.then: Callable that receives the PNG bytes or `None`.

pyzed.Command.capture_window.desc: Captures what the window shows and calls `then(png)` with its PNG bytes (`then(None)` when it could not be captured). The app draws the window again into an image, so it works the same on every system, even when other windows cover it.

params.then: Callable that receives the PNG bytes or `None`.

pyzed.Command.pick_files.desc: Opens the system's file dialog and calls `then(paths)` with the chosen paths (an empty list when it is cancelled).

params.then: Callable that receives the list of paths.
params.title: The dialog's title.
params.filters: A list of `(name, extensions)` pairs, like `[("Images", ["png", "jpg"])]`.

pyzed.Command.save_file.desc: Opens the system's "Save as" dialog and calls `then(paths)` with the chosen path in a list (an empty list when it is cancelled).

params.then: Callable that receives the list with the path.
params.title: The dialog's title.
params.filters: A list of `(name, extensions)` pairs, like `[("Images", ["png", "jpg"])]`.

pyzed.Command.open_window.desc: Opens a new window for that `pz.Window` instance.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.drag_window.desc: Starts moving the window with the mouse (use it when a custom title bar is pressed).

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.
The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.toggle_maximize_window.desc: Maximizes the window, or restores it if it already is.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.maximize_window.desc: Maximizes the window, or restores it with `maximized=False`.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.drag_resize_window.desc: Starts resizing the window with the mouse from an edge or corner (for windows without system decorations; `ui.window_frame` and `pz.window_edges` already do it).

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.show_window_menu.desc: Shows the system's window menu (move, size, close…) under the pointer. Only Windows has one.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.set_fullscreen.desc: Enters or leaves fullscreen, on a chosen screen and maybe exclusive. See [Screens and kiosks](/pyzed/guides/windows/#screens-and-kiosks).

params.fullscreen: `True` for fullscreen, `False` back to a window.
params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.
params.monitor: An index of `pz.monitors()`; `None` keeps the current screen.
params.exclusive: `True` takes the screen over with its own video mode (lower latency on Windows and X11; Wayland keeps a borderless window).

pyzed.Command.set_window_level.desc: Keeps the window above or below the others.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.hide_cursor.desc: Hides the pointer over the window whatever the widgets ask (touch panels, kiosks).

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.list_monitors.desc: Asks the system for its screens and calls `then(monitors)` with a list of `pz.Monitor` (also kept for `pz.monitors()`).

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.move_window.desc: Moves the window to a position on the screen.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.focus_window.desc: Brings the window to the front and focuses it.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pages.title: Core widgets
pages.description: API reference for Pyzed's native widgets: layout, text, controls, the code editor, SVG and icons, all rendered in Rust by Iced.
pages.intro:
The core widgets are implemented in Rust and imported from `pyzed`. They are the
building blocks of the [components](/pyzed/components/overview/).
See the [layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/) guide for sizes, padding and colors.

pyzed.Widget.desc:
An immutable node of the UI tree, implemented in Rust. Returned by every widget and component function. Wherever a child is expected you can also pass a string or a number (converted to `text`) or `None` (ignored).

Every widget has `widget.on(...)` (see [Events](/pyzed/guides/events/)) and `widget.style(*styles, **props)`, which styles it like CSS: background, borders, radius, shadow, padding, margin, size and the typography of every text inside. `widget.style_props()` returns what was set. `widget.classes(*names, id=None)` applies the matching rules of `pz.stylesheet`, like HTML's `class` and `id`. See [Styles](/pyzed/theming/styles/).

`widget.animate(*animations, **options)` plays presets or keyframe animations (on mount, hover, press, focus, click or while `active`) and `widget.transition(**props)` animates property changes like a CSS transition. See [Animation](/pyzed/animation/).

pyzed.container.desc: Wraps a child to give it size, alignment, background, border, radius and shadow.

params.content: The child (or `None` for an empty box, handy as a colored rectangle).
params.center: Centers the content on both axes and fills all the space.

pyzed.center.desc: Centers `content` in all the available space. Equivalent to `container(content, center=True)`.

params.anchor_bottom: Keeps the scroll pinned to the end (logs, terminals, chats).
params.margin: Margin between the scrollbar and the content.
params.on_scroll: Callable that receives a dict with `x`, `y`, `relative_x`, `relative_y`, `width`, `height`, `content_width` and `content_height`.

pyzed.stack.desc: Layers its children on top of each other, the last one on top. The basis for layers, modals and notifications.

pyzed.space.desc: Empty space of a given size.

pyzed.hspace.desc: Flexible horizontal gap: pushes the siblings in a row towards the edges.

pyzed.vspace.desc: Flexible vertical gap: pushes the siblings in a column towards the edges.

pyzed.rule.extra: A horizontal rule fills the full width. Inside a column that should shrink, set `width="shrink"` on the column.

pyzed.grid.desc: Lays out its children in a grid. With `columns=3` the columns are equal (or `max_width` fits as many as possible). With track lists (`columns=[200, "1fr", "auto"]`, `rows=...`) it works like a CSS grid: numbers are pixels, `"auto"` fits the content and `"<n>fr"` shares the space left. Wrap children in `pz.cell` to place them and make them span; the rest fill the free cells row by row. See [Layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/#grids).

params.columns: Number of equal columns, or tracks: a list (`[200, "1fr", "auto"]`) or a string (`"200 1fr auto"`).
params.rows: Row tracks, like `columns`. Rows beyond the list are `"auto"`.
params.height: With `columns=<int>`: height of each row. With tracks: the grid's height.
params.width: With `columns=<int>`: pixels. With tracks: the grid's width (default `"fill"`).
params.aspect_ratio: Keeps cells at this width/height ratio (`columns=<int>` only).
params.max_width: Fits as many columns of at most this width as possible (`columns=<int>` only).
params.align_x: Horizontal alignment of items in their cells: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`.
params.align_y: Vertical alignment of items in their cells.

pyzed.grid.example:
pz.grid([pz.cell(header, column=0, row=0, column_span=2), sidebar, content],
        columns=[200, "1fr"], rows=[48, "1fr"], spacing=8, height="fill")

pyzed.cell.desc: Places a child in a track grid: its column and row (from 0) and how many it spans. Children without a cell fill the free cells row by row. Outside a grid it is just the child.

pyzed.box.desc: A container for anything, like an HTML `div`: it lays out its children (`display` `"block"`, `"flex"`, `"grid"` or `"stack"`) and takes every style property, stylesheet classes and an id. Children styled with `position="absolute"` are placed by `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left` above the rest. See [Boxes](/pyzed/guides/layout/#boxes).

params.children: The widgets, one by one or in lists. `None` and `False` are skipped.
params.display: `"block"` (one under another, as wide as the box), `"flex"`, `"grid"` or `"stack"`.
params.wrap: With `"flex"` rows: wraps onto new lines.
params.columns: With `"grid"`: a count of equal columns or tracks (`"200 1fr auto"`).
params.class_: Stylesheet classes (`"card selected"` or a list).
params.props: Style properties, on top of the rest.

pyzed.box.example: pz.box(title, pz.box(cancel, save, display="flex", justify="end", gap=8), class_="card", gap=12)

pyzed.flex.desc: Lays children out along one axis, like CSS flexbox, with `justify` on the main axis and `align` on the cross axis. Use `pz.flex_item` to make a child grow or give it a fixed size.

params.children: The widgets, or `pz.flex_item(...)` for children with their own sizing.
params.justify: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, `"between"`, `"around"` or `"evenly"`. No effect when a child grows.
params.wrap: Wraps onto new lines (rows with `justify="start"` only).

pyzed.flex.example: pz.flex([logo, title, pz.flex_item(search, grow=1), avatar], justify="between", align="center", gap=8)

params.grow: Share of the free space on the main axis (`0` keeps its natural size).
params.basis: A fixed main size in pixels, instead of growing.

pyzed.anchor.desc: Places a child of `pz.anchor_layout` at `x`, `y` with `width` and `height` (in the layout's design size) and says how it follows a resize.

params.x: Left edge in the design size.
params.y: Top edge in the design size.
params.anchor: A preset of `pyzed.anchors.PRESETS` (`"top_right"`, `"bottom_wide"`, `"center"`, `"full"`...), words (`"left right bottom"`) or a tuple of edges.
params.min_width: Smallest width when it stretches (`0`: no limit).
params.max_width: Largest width when it stretches (`0`: no limit).
params.pivot: `(x, y)` from `0` to `1`: the point that stays put when a limit stops it, and that `rotate` turns around.

pyzed.anchor.example: pz.anchor(ui.button("Close", on_close), x=284, y=252, width=100, height=32, anchor="bottom_right")

pyzed.anchor_layout.desc: Places children made with `pz.anchor` freely, like a designed form: when it is resized, each child keeps its distance to the edges it is anchored to, stretches between opposite ones and stays centered otherwise. Later children are drawn on top. See [Anchored layouts](/pyzed/guides/layout/#anchored-layouts).

params.design: `(width, height)` the children were laid out in; by default the smallest size that holds them.

pyzed.anchor_layout.example:
pz.anchor_layout([
    pz.anchor(ui.heading("Report"), x=16, y=12, width=368, height=28, anchor="top_wide"),
    pz.anchor(ui.button("Close", on_close), x=284, y=252, width=100, height=32, anchor="bottom_right"),
], design=(400, 300))

pyzed.anchors.place.desc: Where a box designed in a parent of size `design` goes in a parent of size `actual`, following its anchor, with size limits and a pivot. The math behind `pz.anchor_layout` and designed forms.

params.rect: `(x, y, width, height)` in the design size.
params.pivot: The point that stays put when a limit stops the box from stretching.

pyzed.anchors.PRESETS.desc: The 16 anchor presets by name (`top_left`, `top_center`, `top_right`, `top_wide`, `center_left`, `center`, `center_right`, `center_wide`, `bottom_left`, `bottom_center`, `bottom_right`, `bottom_wide`, `left_tall`, `center_tall`, `right_tall`, `full`), each the tuple of edges it anchors to.

pyzed.anchors.edges.desc: The edges of an anchor given as a preset name, words or edges. Raises `ValueError` for anything else.

pyzed.anchors.preset_of.desc: The name of the preset a set of edges matches (every set is one of the 16).

pyzed.anchors.axes.desc: The `(horizontal, vertical)` placement of a set of edges, such as `("right", "top")`.

pyzed.anchors.snap_to.desc: A box moved (and sized, on stretched axes) to sit where an anchor points: against the anchored edges, centered or filling the parent, `margin` pixels in.

pyzed.anchors.offsets.desc: The distances `(left, top, right, bottom)` from each side of the parent to a box.

pyzed.anchors.pivot_offset.desc: The translation that makes a rotation and a scale (which turn around a box's center) turn around `pivot` instead.

pyzed.focusable.desc: Lets any widget take the keyboard focus like a text field: a click or Tab focuses it (`Command.focus(id)` too) and, while it has it, the combos in `keys` call `on_key(combo)` instead of reaching the app's `on_key`. A ring is drawn around it once the keyboard is used on it. The library's switches, check boxes, sliders, segmented controls and radio groups use it.

params.on_key: Called with the combo (`"space"`, `"shift-right"`…) of each key in `keys` pressed while it has the focus. `None` leaves `content` unfocusable.
params.keys: The combos it takes (by default Space, Enter, the arrows, Home and End); `"*"` takes every key. Tab is left to move the focus.
params.ring_color: Color of the focus ring (none by default).
params.ring_offset: Pixels between the control and the ring.
params.tab_index: Its place (and that of every field inside it) in the order Tab moves the focus in: lower numbers first, then the fields without one, in the order they are drawn. Works without `on_key` too.

pyzed.focusable.example: pz.focusable(stars, lambda combo: self.rate(+1 if combo == "right" else -1), keys=["left", "right"], ring_color="#528bff")

pyzed.window_edges.desc: Wraps the whole view of a window without system decorations so that pressing near its edges resizes the window (the corners take twice as much room). `ui.window_frame` already uses it.

params.border: Width in pixels of the area that resizes.
params.enabled: `False` turns it off (for a maximized window).

pyzed.resizable.desc: A panel whose `edge` can be dragged to resize it. It keeps the size the user drags it to; `on_resize(size)` is called when a drag ends so you can save it. Changing `size` later resets it.

params.edge: The edge with the handle: `"right"` (a left sidebar), `"left"`, `"top"` (a bottom panel) or `"bottom"`.
params.on_resize: Called with the new size when a drag ends.
params.hover_color: Line color while hovered or dragged.
params.handle: Width of the area that can be grabbed.

pyzed.split.desc: Two panes with a draggable divider. For the theme style use `ui.split`.

params.ratio: Proportion of the first pane (0–1). The split keeps the ratio the user drags to until this changes.
params.on_resize: Callable that receives the new ratio while dragging.
params.min_size: Minimum size of the first pane.
params.min_size_second: Minimum size of the second pane.
params.hover_color: Divider color on hover or while dragging.

pyzed.pin.desc: Places `content` at `(x, y)` inside a box. Use it in a `stack` to position popovers and context menus.

pyzed.responsive.desc: Builds its content with `function(width, height)` using the space actually available, so the layout can adapt (for example, hiding a sidebar when the window is narrow).

params.function: Function that receives `(width, height)` and returns a widget.

params.font: `"sans"` (IBM Plex Sans), `"mono"`, `"icons"`, `"serif"` or the name of a family loaded with `load_font`.
params.line_height: Line height relative to the size (1.0, 1.5…).
params.wrap: Line wrapping. With `False` the text doesn't wrap.
params.selectable: `True` lets the mouse select the text (drag, double-click a word, triple-click a block) and Ctrl+C copy it. A string names a selection group: the texts and Markdown of one group form a single selection, in the order they are drawn (the lines of a log, the messages of a chat).

pyzed.icon.desc: A [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icon. `color` defaults to the surrounding text color.

params.source: Path to an `.svg`, the SVG code as a string (starting with `<`) or `bytes`.
params.color: If given, tints the whole SVG with that color (useful for monochrome icons).

pyzed.image.desc: A bitmap image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP…) from a path or `bytes`, or raw RGBA pixels.

params.size: `(width, height)` when `source` is raw RGBA pixels.
params.background: Decode on a worker thread: `None` (the default) does it for files of 256 KB and up, `True` always, `False` never. Until it is ready the image shows nothing, so give it a `width` and `height` to keep its space.

pyzed.image_viewer.desc: An image you can pan (by dragging) and zoom (mouse wheel), like Iced's viewer.

params.scale_step: How much the zoom changes per wheel step.

pyzed.markdown.desc: Renders Markdown (headings, lists, code blocks, quotes, tables, links…). For the theme colors use `ui.markdown`.

params.on_link: Callable that receives the URL when a link is clicked.
params.selectable: `True` lets the mouse select the text (drag, double-click a word, triple-click a block) and Ctrl+C copy it. A string names a selection group: the texts and Markdown of one group form a single selection, in the order they are drawn (the lines of a log, the messages of a chat).

pyzed.rich_text.desc: Text made of spans with different styles. Plain strings are unstyled spans.
pyzed.rich_text.example: pz.rich_text(["Click ", pz.span("here", color="#74ade8", underline=True, link=self.open), " to open."])

pyzed.span.desc: A styled span for `rich_text`. With `link`, clicking it sends (or calls) that value.

pyzed.Span.desc: The type of the spans created by `pz.span`.

params.data: The text or URL to encode.
params.cell_size: Size of each module in pixels.

pyzed.shader.desc: A widget painted on the GPU by your WGSL `fn shade(uv, px, size, time) -> vec4<f32>`, which returns each pixel's color, or by a shader graph made of nodes (a `.pzshad` path or a [`pyzed.shading`](/pyzed/reference/shading/) `Graph` or `Shader`). Each entry of `uniforms` becomes a function of the same name (`{"speed": 2}` -> `speed()`); `mouse()` gives the pointer. Without a GPU the widget shows `fallback`. Raises `ValueError` with the compiler's message for invalid code. See the [shaders](/pyzed/shading/shaders/) guide.

params.code: WGSL source that defines `shade` (and any helper functions), or a `.pzshad` path, `Graph` or `Shader`.
params.uniforms: Up to 32 named values: a number, 2 to 4 numbers or a color. With a `.pzshad`, the shader's mutable variables by name.
params.textures: Up to 8 images, `{name: path}`: each becomes `name(uv)`, the image's color at `uv`.
params.time: A fixed `time` in seconds, for a still frame.
params.fallback: Color or gradient shown without a GPU.

pyzed.canvas.desc: A 2D drawing surface. `shapes` is a list created with [`pyzed.draw`](/pyzed/reference/draw/). Mouse callbacks receive coordinates relative to the canvas. With an `id`, the geometry is cached between frames and only recomputed when the shapes change. See the [drawing with canvas](/pyzed/guides/canvas/) guide.

params.shapes: List of `pyzed.draw` shapes (nested lists are accepted).
params.on_press: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on press.
params.on_release: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on release.
params.on_right_press: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on right click.
params.on_scroll: Callable that receives `(dx, dy)` in lines when the wheel is used.

pyzed.button.desc: A button with no predefined style. For the themed button use `ui.button`.

pyzed.text_input.desc: A controlled text field: it shows `value` and notifies you of changes through `on_input`. For the themed field use `ui.input`.

pyzed.mouse_area.desc: Detects mouse events over its content.

params.on_scroll: Callable that receives `(dx, dy)` in lines when the wheel is used.

pyzed.hover.desc: Shows `top` over `base` only while the mouse is over it (for example, a tab's close button).

pyzed.opaque.desc: Makes a widget block the mouse for whatever is below it in a `stack`.

pyzed.tooltip.desc: Shows `tip` next to `content` on hover. `ui.tooltip` adds the theme's style.

pyzed.popup.desc: Shows `content` over everything else next to `base`, like the menu of a drop-down: it is not cut off by the panels `base` sits in, flips to the other side when it does not fit and stays inside the window. A press outside it (and outside `base`) or Escape calls `on_dismiss`. With `content=None` only `base` is shown. The date pickers open their calendars with it.

params.base: The widget it belongs to (a field, a button).
params.content: What opens (a panel, a menu), or `None` while closed.
params.on_dismiss: Message or callable sent on a press outside or Escape.
params.align: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`: how it lines up with `base`.

pyzed.popup.example: pz.popup(field, panel if self.open else None, on_dismiss=self.close)

params.on_release: Sent when the knob is released.

pyzed.pick_list.desc: A dropdown to choose one of `options`. `on_select(option)` receives the chosen one. For the themed dropdown use `ui.select`. It takes the keyboard focus like a text field (a click, Tab or `Command.focus(id)`) and keeps it after a choice: ↑/↓ then pick the previous or next option without opening it, Home/End the first and last and typing jumps to an option; Enter, Space, Alt+↓ or F4 open the menu, where ↑/↓ move, Enter picks and Esc closes.

params.focus_border_color: Border color while it has the keyboard focus.

pyzed.radio.desc: A radio button. Group several yourself (or use `ui.radio_group`); `on_select` is sent when it is clicked.

params.spacing: Space between the circle and the text.

pyzed.code_editor.desc:
A code editor with syntax highlighting, line numbers and git markers, based on Iced's
`text_editor`. It is **uncontrolled**: `text` is only the initial value for that `id`; the
text, cursor and history live in Rust. Use `Command.set_editor_text` to replace it.
For the themed editor use [`ui.editor`](/pyzed/components/code/).

params.id: Identifies the buffer. Reuse it to keep state across renders.
params.syntax: Map of TextMate scopes to colors (provided by `Theme.syntax_scopes()`).
params.gutter_active_color: Color of the cursor line's number.
params.markers: `{line: color}` for git markers in the gutter (lines from 1).
params.on_change: Callable that receives the full text after each edit.
params.annotations: `{line: "text"}` or `{line: ("text", color)}`: virtual text at the end of the line (code lens, diagnostics).
params.whitespace: Draws spaces as `·` and tabs as `→` in this color.
params.tab_size: Tab inserts spaces up to the next multiple; Enter keeps the indentation; Backspace removes a level.
params.hard_tabs: With `tab_size`: Tab, Enter and indent (Ctrl+]) use tab characters instead of spaces.
params.backspace_unindent: With `tab_size`: Backspace in leading spaces removes a whole level (`False`: one space).
params.repeat_delay: Milliseconds Backspace and Delete wait, held down, before repeating (`None`: the system's).
params.repeat_rate: Deletions per second at most while Backspace or Delete is held down (`None`: the system's pace).
params.capture_keys: Keys the editor leaves to the app's `on_key` (`"up"`, `"enter"`…), e.g. while a completion list is open.
params.auto_close: Typing a bracket or quote also inserts its closing pair.
params.folding: Fold chevrons in the gutter and Ctrl+Shift+[ / ].
params.minimap: Width of the minimap in pixels (`None`: no minimap).
params.minimap_thumb: Color of the minimap's visible-area highlight.
params.on_zoom: Callable that receives `1`, `-1` or `0` for Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+wheel.
params.on_action: Callable that receives the name of each editor action that runs (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`…).
params.on_paste: Called after Ctrl+V (Cmd+V, Shift+Insert) pastes the clipboard's text, if it holds any: a chat box reads an image from the clipboard with `Command.paste_image`.
params.highlights: Ranges painted behind the text (search results): `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.
params.match_brackets: Outlines the bracket that matches the one next to the cursor.
params.selection_highlight: Highlights the other occurrences of the selected text.
params.keymap: Zed-style `{binding: action}` dict; `None` as the action removes a default key (`pyzed.ui.editor.keymap_for` builds one from per-action overrides).
params.readonly: `True` lets the text be selected and copied but not changed (a log, a traceback).
params.on_hover: Callable that receives `{line, column, start, end, x, y, height}` (the word under the mouse, from 1, and its place in the editor) after the mouse rests on it, and `None` when it leaves (hover cards).
params.hover_delay: Milliseconds the mouse rests on a word before `on_hover` is called.
params.sticky_scroll: How many lines of the enclosing blocks (`class`, `def`, `if`…) stay pinned at the top while scrolling (`0`: none).
params.indent_guides: Colors of the indent guides, one per depth (they repeat); none: no guides.
params.indent_guides_active: Colors of the guide of the block around the cursor, by depth like `indent_guides`.

pyzed.Style.desc: A reusable set of style properties for `widget.style(...)`, a component's `style=` or `App.style`. Combine styles with `|` (the right one wins). See [Styles](/pyzed/theming/styles/).

params.styles: Styles, dicts or style names to start from.
params.props: Properties: `background`, `color`, `font`, `weight`, `italic`, `size`, `line_height`, `border_color`, `border_width`, `border` (`(width, color)`), `radius`, `shadow`, `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `align_x`, `align_y`, `clip`. Effects: `opacity`, `translate` (`(x, y)`, pixels or `"50%"`), `scale`, `glow` (a color, a size or `(color, size)`), `bloom` (a color or `(color, intensity)`) and `glass` (`True`, a tint or `{"tint", "strength"}`). States: `hover`, `pressed` (or `active`) and `focus`, each with the properties to show then. `transition`: milliseconds, `True` or `{"duration", "easing", "delay"}`. `media`: `{query: style}` applied when the window matches. Colors may be theme tokens.

pyzed.Style.example:
card = pz.Style(background="panel", border=(1, "border"), radius=8, padding=12)
pz.column([...]).style(card | pz.Style(shadow=("#0006", (0, 4), 12)))

pyzed.define_style.desc: Names a style so widgets can use it by name: `widget.style("card")`. Returns it.

pyzed.stylesheet.desc: Adds CSS-like rules, `{selector: style}`, that widgets get with `widget.classes(...)` and components with `class_=`/`id=`. Selectors: `.class`, `.a.b`, `#id`, a component's class name (`"Rating"`), an optional `:hover`, `:pressed`/`:active` or `:focus`, and comma lists. More specific selectors win (ids, then classes, then names), then later rules. A selector given again replaces its rule. Returns every rule. See [Stylesheets](/pyzed/theming/styles/#stylesheets).

pyzed.media.desc: Whether the window being drawn matches a media query, like CSS `@media`. See [Responsive styles](/pyzed/theming/styles/#responsive-styles).
pyzed.media.example: sidebar = None if pz.media("max_width: 600") else self.sidebar()

pyzed.viewport.desc: The size of the window being drawn, `(width, height)` in logical pixels, like `window.innerWidth` and `innerHeight`.

pyzed.current_breakpoint.desc: The widest breakpoint the window reaches: `"xs"` (under 640 px), `"sm"`, `"md"`, `"lg"`, `"xl"` or `"xxl"`.

pyzed.set_style.desc: Sets the global style for every window, under each window's `style`. Without arguments it clears it.

pyzed.Gradient.desc: A linear gradient for backgrounds. Angles follow CSS: 0 up, 90 right, 180 (the default) down. Up to 8 stops.

params.stops: Colors, spread evenly, or `(offset, color)` pairs with offsets from 0 to 1.

pyzed.Mask.desc: An opacity mask for a `Paint`: how visible the fill is along a direction. On a gradient it follows the gradient's direction.

params.stops: Opacities (0 to 1), spread evenly, or `(offset, opacity)` pairs.
params.angle: Direction when the fill is a plain color.

pyzed.Paint.desc: A fill: a color or `Gradient` with an overall opacity and an optional `Mask`. Works anywhere a background does.

params.opacity: 0 to 1, multiplies the fill's own alpha.

pyzed.Paint.example: pz.Paint("#3b82f6", opacity=0.8, mask=pz.Mask([1, 0]))  # fades out downwards

pyzed.animation.PRESETS.desc: Every named animation (the built-in presets and the ones added with `define_animation`), mapped to its `Animation`. See [the preset list](/pyzed/animation/presets/).

pyzed.animation.EASINGS.desc: Easing names (`linear`, `ease`, `ease_out_cubic`, `ease_out_back`, `spring`...). `animate()` also takes `(x1, y1, x2, y2)` cubic Béziers and `"steps(n)"`.

pyzed.animation.TRIGGERS.desc: What plays an animation: `mount`, `hover`, `press`, `focus`, `click`, `active` and `manual` (each time `key` changes; a `pz.Trigger` given to `on=` uses it).

pyzed.animation.PROPERTIES.desc: The properties animations and transitions change: `opacity`, `x`, `y`, `scale`, `background`, `border_color`, `color`, `radius`, `border_width`, `glow` and `glow_color`.

pyzed.animation.WINDOW_TRANSITIONS.desc: Names for `Window.transition` (`fade`, `zoom`, `pop`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`) mapped to their `(opening, closing)` presets.

pyzed.virtual_column.desc: A column of `count` rows of the same height that only builds the rows in view: `item(index)` is called when row `index` scrolls into view, and rows that leave it are dropped. A column of a million rows costs the same as one of fifty. Put it in a `scrollable` (it virtualizes against the visible area of the closest one, or the window).

params.item: Function that receives a row index and returns its widget.
params.item_height: Height of every row, in pixels.
params.overscan: Extra rows built above and below the visible ones, so fast scrolling shows no gaps.

pyzed.virtual_column.example:
rows = load_logs()          # a list with 500 000 entries

pz.scrollable(
    pz.virtual_column(len(rows), lambda i: pz.text(rows[i]), item_height=20),
    id="logs", height="fill",
)

pyzed.memo.desc: Decorator that caches what a view function returns by its arguments, so the next `view()` reuses the same widget tree while they don't change. Pass everything the subtree depends on as arguments. Lists, dicts and sets compare by contents, other unhashable objects by identity; the current theme and language are always part of the key. `function.cache_clear()` empties its cache.

params.function: The function to memoize (when used as `@pz.memo`).
params.maxsize: How many results to keep per function (least recently used are dropped).

pyzed.clear_memos.desc: Empties the cache of every `@pz.memo` function.

pyzed.memo_stats.desc: Returns `{"hits": n, "misses": m}`: how many calls of memoized functions were answered from the cache and how many built their result.

pages.title: Components (pyzed.ui)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.ui: every ready-made component, its parameters, defaults and events, for building native Python desktop apps.
pages.intro:
Signatures and parameters of every component. To see them with images and examples,
go to the [Components](/pyzed/components/overview/) section.

They are all functions that return a `Widget` and read their colors from the current theme.
Color parameters accept a theme **token** (`"accent"`, `"text_muted"`,
`"error"`…) or a hex color.

params.color: Theme token or hex color. Defaults to `"text"`.

pyzed.ui.button.desc: A themed button with variants, sizes, an icon and a shortcut.

params.loading: Shows a spinner in place of the icon and ignores presses (keep a `pz.every(1/30, ...)` subscription while it spins).

pyzed.ui.icon_button.desc: A square button with just an icon.

params.name: Icon name.
params.keys: Key binding shown in the tooltip.
params.loading: Swaps the icon for a spinner and ignores presses.
params.indicator: Adds a small dot in this color at the top right (unread, changes…).

pyzed.ui.badge.desc: A small pill for statuses and counters.

pyzed.ui.indicator.desc: A colored dot (status, unsaved changes, presence).

pyzed.ui.kbd.desc: Draws a shortcut as keys: `"ctrl-shift-p"`, `"cmd-k cmd-s"`. Uses symbols on macOS (⌘⇧P) and words elsewhere.

pyzed.ui.format_keys.desc: Splits a shortcut into labels per chord: `format_keys("ctrl-shift-p") == [["Ctrl", "Shift", "P"]]`. The style is controlled by `pyzed.ui.base.KEY_STYLE` (`"auto"`, `"symbols"` or `"words"`).

pyzed.ui.keys_text.desc: A shortcut as plain text for a label or a status line: `keys_text("ctrl-shift-p") == "Ctrl+Shift+P"` (`"⌃⇧P"` with macOS symbols), chords separated by a space. Tooltips, buttons and menus take `keys=` instead and draw key caps, so never write the keys into their text.

params.index: Picks a collaborator color from the theme (`theme.players`).
params.image: A picture (path or bytes) instead of the initials.
params.tooltip: Text shown on hover (the person's name).

pyzed.ui.tooltip.desc: Wraps `content` with a themed tooltip, optionally with its shortcut.

pyzed.ui.divider.desc: A divider line in the theme color.

params.label: Muted text in the middle of a horizontal line (`"or"`, a date…).
params.spacing: Space on both sides of the line.

pyzed.ui.card.desc: A bordered surface to group content, with an optional title and actions.

params.selected: Outlines it in the accent color.

pyzed.ui.input.desc: A text field. Focus, blur and keys come from the common events: `.on(focus=..., blur=..., key_down=...)`.

params.borderless: No border or background (as in the command palette).
params.disabled: Greys it out and ignores typing.
params.readonly: Selectable and copyable, but it can't be changed.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.
params.on_clear: Shows an ✕ while there is text; sent when it is clicked.

pyzed.ui.search_input.desc: An `input` with a magnifying glass icon.

pyzed.ui.path_input.desc: A text field for a file or folder path with a button that opens the system's file dialog, so the path never has to be typed (it still can be).

params.on_change: Callable that receives the typed or chosen path.
params.folder: Picks a folder instead of a file.
params.directory: Folder the dialog opens in (by default, the current path's).
params.relative_to: A chosen path inside this folder is given relative to it.
params.title: Title of the dialog.
params.placeholder: Text shown while it is empty.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

params.disabled: Greys it out and ignores clicks.

pyzed.ui.checkbox.desc: A checkbox. `checked=None` shows the mixed state (part of a group checked); clicking it checks it.

params.disabled: Greys it out and ignores clicks.

params.on_release: Sent when the drag ends (save or apply there).
params.show_value: Shows the number next to it: `True`, or a format such as `"{:.0%}"`.

params.value: Progress, or `None` for an indeterminate bar (keep a `pz.every(1/30, ...)` subscription while it shows).
params.label: Text above the bar.
params.show_value: Adds the percentage at its right.

pyzed.ui.segmented.desc: A group of mutually exclusive buttons.

pyzed.ui.field.desc: A form row: title and description on the left, control on the right (like a settings screen).

params.error: A validation message shown under the title in the error color (see `pz.validation_errors`).
params.required: Adds a red `*` after the title.
params.vertical: Puts the control under the title.

pyzed.ui.dialog_layer.desc: Shows a dialog centered over `base` with a dimmed backdrop. With `dialog=None` it returns `base` unchanged, so it can always wrap the view. See [Dialogs](/pyzed/guides/i18n/#dialogs).

params.dialog: A dialog from the functions below, or `ui.modal`.
params.on_dismiss: Sent when the backdrop is clicked.

pyzed.ui.dialog_layer.example:
ui.dialog_layer(self.main_view(), ui.confirm("Delete 3 files?", self.delete, self.cancel, danger=True)
                if self.asking else None, on_dismiss=self.cancel)

params.on_close: The button and the close icon.

params.danger: Paints the confirm button red and labels it Delete.

pyzed.ui.prompt.desc: Asks for a line of text.

pyzed.ui.choice.desc: A message with your own buttons.

params.options: `(label, on_press)` pairs; the last one is the main button.

pyzed.ui.unsaved_changes.desc: "Save your changes to *name* before closing?" with Don't save, Cancel and Save.

pyzed.ui.select.desc: A dropdown with the theme style. Options are displayed with `str()`, so strings, enums, dataclasses or database models all work; `on_select` receives the chosen object, not its label.

params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.radio_group.desc: Mutually exclusive options as radio buttons.

params.on_select: Callable that receives the chosen value.
params.horizontal: In a row instead of a column.
params.descriptions: Maps values to a muted line under their label.

pyzed.ui.number_field.desc: A numeric field with −/+ buttons that you can also drag, like Figma's. `on_change(value)` receives the number already clamped to `min`/`max`; anything that can't be parsed as a number is ignored. Press and move the mouse sideways over the number to change it (it keeps going outside the window); double-click it to type a value, and Enter, Escape or a click outside to finish. Once clicked, ↑/↓ step it (Shift: ten steps) and Home/End jump to `min`/`max`.

params.steppers: Shows the −/+ buttons (`False`: a compact field, as in a property grid).
params.drag: Lets the mouse change it by dragging (`False`: a plain text field).
params.drag_step: How much each pixel dragged adds (by default `step`, up to 1; steps under 1 take three pixels each).
params.align: Where the number sits between the buttons: `"center"` (default), `"start"` or `"end"`.
params.decimals: Decimals shown (by default, as many as `step`).
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.split_button.desc: A button with a separate arrow for more options. `on_press` runs the main action and `on_menu` usually opens a `ui.menu` in a `ui.popover`.

params.multiple: Each button toggles its value on or off.

pyzed.ui.chip.desc: A compact tag, optionally clickable (filters) and with a button to remove it.

params.on_remove: Shows a ✕ that sends this when clicked.
params.disabled: Greys it out and ignores presses.

pyzed.ui.disclosure.desc: A collapsible section: a header with an arrow that shows or hides `content`. You own the open state: change it in `on_toggle`.

params.title: Title (text or widget).
params.on_toggle: Message or callable when the header is clicked.

pyzed.ui.AccordionSection.desc: One section of `ui.accordion`: `key`, `title`, `content` and optional `icon` and header `end` widget.

pyzed.ui.accordion.desc: Stacked collapsible sections separated by dividers, like the panels of a settings screen. Each header spans the whole width, so the content lines up with the rest of the panel. You own the open state: change it in `on_toggle`.

params.sections: `ui.AccordionSection(key, title, content, icon=None, end=None)` items (or `(key, title, content)` tuples).
params.open: The set of open ids, a `{id: bool}` dict, or `True` for all.
params.on_toggle: Called with the key of the clicked header.
params.icons: `{id: icon}`: a Lucide icon for each header.
params.spacing: Space around the dividers between sections.
params.padding: Padding around the content of an open section.

pyzed.ui.accordion.example:
ui.accordion([
    ui.AccordionSection("layout", "Layout", layout_rows, icon="ruler"),
    ui.AccordionSection("events", "Events", event_rows, icon="zap"),
], open=self.open_sections, on_toggle=lambda key: self.open_sections.symmetric_difference_update({key}))

pyzed.ui.Log.desc: The entries of a `ui.console`: thread-safe, capped at `limit`, with repeated lines folded into one. `write(level, text)` adds a line; `capture()` (or `with log:`) copies `print` output and tracebacks into it; `pipe(stream)` reads a subprocess's output in a background thread; `text()` returns everything for copying (`text(ids)` only those lines). `write` also takes the line's `source`, `detail` (a traceback) and `origin` (`(path, line)`) and returns the entry; `find(id)` looks one up.

params.on_write: Called after every write (from any thread).

pyzed.ui.Log.example:
log = ui.Log()
with log:
    print("hello")          # still reaches the terminal
ui.console(log.entries, on_clear=log.clear)

pyzed.ui.LogEntry.desc: One line of a `ui.Log`: `level`, `text`, `time`, `count` (identical lines in a row), `source`, `detail`, `origin`, its number `id`, `clock` (`HH:MM:SS`) and `line()` (the entry as plain text).

params.source: What it comes from (`"project"`, `"agent"`...); `ui.console` can show and filter it.
params.detail: More text shown under the line while it is selected (a traceback).
params.origin: `(path, line)` of the code it is about.
params.id: Its number in the log (what a `ui.LogSelection` keeps).

pyzed.ui.LogSelection.desc: The selected lines of a `ui.console`, like in a file list: a click selects one line, Shift+click a range from the last one clicked and Ctrl+click (Cmd on macOS) adds or removes one. Keep one in your app and pass it to `ui.console(selection=...)`; `select(ids)` selects exactly those (Ctrl+A), `clear()` none, `keep(entries)` forgets lines that are gone, and `ids` are the selected entries' `id`s for `log.text(ids)`.
pyzed.ui.LogSelection.example:
self.selection = ui.LogSelection()
...
ui.console(self.log.entries, selection=self.selection, on_context=self.open_menu)
# Ctrl+C in on_key:
return pz.Command.copy(self.log.text(self.selection.ids))

pyzed.ui.LOG_LEVELS.desc: The levels `ui.console` colors, in the order of its filter buttons: debug, info, event, stdout, stderr, warning, error.

pyzed.ui.console.desc: A log view like a browser's dev tools console: a filter box, one toggle per level with its count, copy and clear, and the entries in a monospace list that keeps scrolling to the newest one.

params.on_query: Receives each edit of the filter.
params.on_toggle_level: Called with the level of the clicked toggle.
params.actions: Extra widgets at the end of the toolbar.
params.selection: A `ui.LogSelection`: the lines can be selected with the mouse, and a selected line with `detail` shows it below.
params.on_context: Called with the line right-clicked (`None` under the lines): open a menu there (copy, go to source, clear...).
params.sources: `(value, label)` pairs: adds a dropdown that shows the lines of one `source`.
params.on_source: Receives the source picked in the dropdown (`None` for all).
params.show_source: Tags each line with its source.
params.placeholder: Text of the empty filter box.
params.empty: What shows while there are no lines.

pyzed.ui.ErrorInfo.desc: An error as `ui.error_card` and `ui.error_dialog` show it: `kind` (the exception's type), `message`, the whole `traceback`, the `origin` `(path, line)` it comes from (the last frame outside the standard library, installed packages and Pyzed), `where` it happened and `time`. `ErrorInfo.from_exception(err, where=...)` makes one (`prefer=` picks which frames may be the origin); `ErrorInfo.current()` describes the exception being handled. `summary` is `Type: message`, `location` is `file.py:12` and `report()` is everything as text for a bug report.

params.traceback: The whole traceback, as Python prints it.
params.origin: `(path, line)` of the code it comes from, or `None`.

pyzed.ui.error_boundary.desc: Draws `build()`, or an error card when it raises, so one part of the view that fails never takes the whole window down (like React's error boundaries). `on_error(info)` is told about the error each time the part is drawn and fails, so report it once (compare `info.traceback`).

params.build: A function that returns the part's widget.
params.title: Heading of the card (and the error's `where`).
params.where: What the part is, for the report.
params.on_details: Adds a Details button; receives the `ui.ErrorInfo` (open a `ui.error_dialog`).
params.fallback: Your own widget for the error: `fallback(info)`.

pyzed.ui.error_boundary.example:
sidebar = ui.error_boundary(lambda: self.sidebar(), on_error=self.report, title="Sidebar",
                            on_details=self.show_error)

pyzed.ui.error_card.desc: The card `ui.error_boundary` draws in place of what failed: the error, where it comes from and a Copy error button (and Details with `on_details`).

pyzed.ui.error_dialog.desc: A dialog with an error: its message, where it happened, the file and line it comes from and the traceback in a read-only editor (select and copy any part), with buttons to copy everything, go to the origin, see it among the logs and close. Show it with `ui.dialog_layer` or `ui.layer`.

params.title: Heading ("Something went wrong").
params.on_go_to: Adds the go-to button (open the file at the line).
params.on_logs: Adds a Show in Logs button.
params.more: How many other errors came after it (a line says so).
params.width: Width in pixels or a modal size.

pyzed.ui.error_dialog.example:
dialog = ui.error_dialog(self.error, self.close_error, on_go_to=self.open_origin) if self.error else None
return ui.dialog_layer(self.main_view(), dialog, on_dismiss=self.close_error)

pyzed.ui.shortcuts.desc: A searchable list of key bindings, grouped (for a Keyboard shortcuts dialog).

pyzed.ui.about.desc: An About box: icon, name, version, a description, a few details and link buttons.

pyzed.ui.callout.desc: An inline notice (a callout or banner).

params.title: Title (text or widget).
params.tint: `"info"`, `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"` or `"hint"`: picks the color and icon.

pyzed.ui.empty_state.desc: A centered placeholder for empty lists, searches with no results, etc.

pyzed.ui.settings_group.desc: A titled block of `ui.field` rows separated by lines, like a settings screen.

params.title: Group title.
params.end: Widget at the right of the title (a Reset button…).

pyzed.ui.Column.desc: A column of `ui.table`. `key` is a dict key, an attribute name or a function of the row; `render` (optional) turns the value into a widget. `width` is `"fill"`, a number or a portion such as `"fill:2"`.

params.title: Header (and name used for sorting).
params.key: How to get the value from each row.
params.sortable: Whether the header can be clicked to sort.

pyzed.ui.table.desc: A data table with a fixed header, optional sorting and row selection. Sorting happens here when `sort_by` names a column: clicking a header calls `on_sort(title)` and you update `sort_by`/`descending` in your state. Rows are virtualized: only the ones in view are built, so hundreds of thousands of rows scroll smoothly.

params.sort_by: Title of the column to sort by.
params.on_sort: Callable that receives the clicked title.
params.on_row_press: Callable that receives the clicked row.
params.selected: The row to highlight, or a list or set of rows (multiple selection).
params.on_row_double_press: Called with the row on a double click (open, edit…).
params.on_row_context: Called with the row on a right click (a context menu).
params.empty: Text or widget shown in place of the rows when there are none.

pyzed.ui.stat.desc: A dashboard number: title, large value, optional change (`+4.2%`) and sparkline.

params.title: Title.
params.delta: Change in %; green if positive, red otherwise.
params.inverse: Colors a drop green and a rise red (errors, latency…).

pyzed.ui.sparkline.desc: A tiny line chart for trends.

params.fill: Fills the area under the line.

pyzed.ui.bar_chart.desc: A vertical bar chart with optional labels.

pyzed.ui.donut.desc: A donut chart; `label` is drawn in the center.

pyzed.ui.spinner.desc: A spinning arc for loading states. Its angle comes from the clock, so keep a `pz.every(1/30, ...)` subscription active while it is shown.

pyzed.ui.count_badge.desc: A round counter (notifications, problems…). Shows `99+` above `max`.

params.show_zero: With `False`, a count of 0 draws nothing.

pyzed.ui.facepile.desc: Overlapping collaborator avatars, as in the title bar of a collaborative editor. Those beyond `max_shown` are grouped into `+N`.

pyzed.ui.keybinding_hint.desc: A muted hint like “Open file Ctrl P” for footers and empty states.

pyzed.ui.markdown.desc: `pz.markdown` with the theme's text, link and code colors.

params.on_link: Callable that receives the URL when a link is clicked.
params.selectable: Same as in `pz.markdown`; the selection uses the theme's `selection` color.

pyzed.ui.split.desc: `pz.split` with the divider in the theme's border color (accent while dragging).

params.on_resize: Callable that receives the new ratio.

pyzed.ui.list_item.desc: A list row: icon, text and a slot at the end.

params.inset: With margin and rounded corners (menus, palettes).
params.description: A muted second line (the row grows to 40 px unless `height` is set).
params.on_double_press: Sent on a double click (open, rename…).

pyzed.ui.TreeNode.desc: A file or folder for `ui.tree`. Folders have `children` (a list). `status` is `"modified"`, `"created"`, `"deleted"`, `"conflict"` or `"ignored"`. `TreeNode.from_paths(paths, status=None)` builds the tree from paths like `"src/main.rs"`, with folders first and the git status propagated to folders.

pyzed.ui.tree.desc: A collapsible file tree, like a code editor's project panel.

params.selected: One id or a collection of ids (multiple selection).
params.on_toggle: Called with the id of the clicked folder.
params.on_select: Called with the id of the clicked file.
params.on_open: Called with the id of a file that is double-clicked.
params.on_context: Called with the id of a row that is right-clicked (show a `ui.menu` there).
params.focused: Outlines the row the keyboard is on.

params.checked: Shows a check mark (`True`/`False`) or nothing (`None`).
params.submenu: Ends the row with a chevron; open the next menu beside it in `on_press`.

pyzed.ui.menu.desc: A floating context menu. Use `ui.SEPARATOR` between groups; a plain string is a header.

params.max_height: Scrolls a menu taller than this.

pyzed.ui.virtual_list.desc: A scrolling list that only builds the rows in view, for thousands or millions of items. `render(item)` returns the widget for one item and is called when it scrolls into view. Every row has the same height.

params.items: The items: a list or any sequence (other iterables are turned into a list).
params.render: Function that receives an item and returns its widget.
params.item_height: Height of every row, in pixels.
params.overscan: Extra rows built above and below the visible ones.
params.on_scroll: Callable that receives the scroll viewport, as in `pz.scrollable`.

pyzed.ui.Tab.desc: A tab. `Tab.for_file(path, **kwargs)` creates it with the file's name and icon.

params.pinned: Shows only the icon, has no close button and goes first in `tab_bar`.
params.tooltip: Text shown on hover (the full path…).

pyzed.ui.tab.desc: A single tab. You normally use `tab_bar`.

params.active: Whether it is the active one.
params.dimmed: Mutes the label (the tab being dragged).

pyzed.ui.tab_bar.desc: A row of tabs with optional controls at the start and end (navigation, split, +). The close button appears on the active tab and on hover. Tabs can be dragged to reorder them or out of the window: see [Draggable tabs](/pyzed/guides/windows/#draggable-tabs-and-detachable-windows).

params.on_drag: Called with the tab id when a tab starts being dragged.
params.on_drop: Called with the tab id and the `Event` when the dragged tab is released: `event.window_x`/`window_y` (outside the window if it was dropped outside) and `event.screen`.
params.on_drag_over: While `dragging` is set: called with the insertion index under the pointer, or `None` when it leaves the bar.
params.dragging: Id of the tab being dragged (dims it and turns on `on_drag_over`).
params.drop_index: Draws the insertion mark before the tab at this index (`len(tabs)`: after the last one).
params.on_context: Called with the id of a tab that is right-clicked.
params.on_new: Sent on a double click of the empty space after the tabs.

pyzed.ui.breadcrumbs.desc: `src › main.rs › fn main`. Parts can be strings or `(icon, text)` tuples.

params.on_press: Called with the index of the clicked part.
params.max_items: Keeps the first part and the last ones and shows `…` for the rest.

pyzed.ui.toolbar.desc: The bar below the tabs: breadcrumbs on the left and buffer actions on the right.

params.center: Kept in the middle of the bar whatever the widths of both sides.

pyzed.ui.workspace.desc: The layout of an editor-style window: title bar, left, right and bottom docks, center and status bar. Pass `None` to hide a dock.

params.on_resize: Called with `(side, size)` when the user finishes resizing a dock by dragging its inner border.

pyzed.ui.title_bar.desc: The top bar: project and branch pickers on the left, account and actions on the right.

pyzed.ui.title_button.desc: A compact button for the title bar (`pyzed ▾`, `main`…).

pyzed.ui.status_item.desc: An icon and/or text in the status bar (diagnostics, cursor position, language…).
