params.led: Color token or hex of a small LED before it (`"success"` for a running server).

pyzed.ui.panel.desc: A dockable panel. `side` decides which edge gets the border line; with a numeric `width` (`height` for the bottom) that border can be dragged to resize it.

params.on_resize: Called with the new size when a drag ends.

pyzed.ui.panel_header.desc: A panel header: icon, title and actions.

pyzed.ui.window_frame.desc: The whole frame of a window opened with `frame="custom"`: a title bar that moves the window (double click maximizes, right click opens the system menu on Windows), the minimize, maximize and close buttons in the style of a platform, menus on the left, and borders that resize the window.

params.content: The window's content, under the title bar.
params.title: Title shown in the bar. By default the window's `title`.
params.menus: Menus on the left of the bar: a list of `ui.Menu`.
params.menu_button: Shows the menus behind a ☰ button (`False` always shows their names).
params.center: Your own widget in the middle instead of the title (a search field, Run and Stop…); the bar still drags on both sides of it.
params.style: `"macos"`, `"windows"`, `"gnome"`, `"ubuntu"` or `"kde"`. By default the window's `frame`, or this system's.
params.window: The window the buttons act on. By default the one whose `view()` is running.
params.height: Height of the bar. By default the platform's.
params.resize_border: Width in pixels of the borders that resize the window.
params.resize_edges: `False` leaves the resize borders to you (`pz.window_edges`), to put them over menus and dialogs.

pyzed.ui.window_title_bar.desc: A window's title bar alone: window buttons in the style of `style` (on the left for macOS), `start` items, the title and `end` items. Without callbacks it only shows, which is how Pyzed Design previews a form in the frame of each platform.

params.title: Title (centered, or on the left on Windows).
params.center: Widget in the middle instead of the title; the bar still drags on both sides of it.
params.on_drag: Called when the empty part of the bar is dragged (return `Command.drag_window()`).
params.on_maximize: Maximize button and double click on the bar.
params.focused: `False` dims it like a window in the background.

pyzed.ui.window_controls.desc: The minimize, maximize and close buttons in the style of a platform. A button without a callback is drawn but does nothing.

pyzed.ui.Menu.desc: A menu of a window frame's menu bar: a name and its items (`ui.MenuItem`, `ui.SEPARATOR` or a header string).

params.label: The menu's name.
params.items: Its entries: `ui.MenuItem`, `ui.SEPARATOR` or a header string.

pyzed.ui.Menu.example: ui.Menu("File", [ui.MenuItem("Open…", self.open, keys="ctrl-o"), ui.SEPARATOR, ui.MenuItem("Quit", self.close)])

pyzed.ui.system_platform.desc: The style of this system's window buttons: `"macos"`, `"windows"`, `"kde"`, `"ubuntu"` or `"gnome"` (other Linux desktops). Under WSL it is `"windows"`.

pyzed.ui.layer.desc: Stacks `overlay` on top of `base`. Clicking outside sends `on_dismiss`. With `overlay=None` it returns `base` unchanged.

params.overlay: What floats on top (modal, palette, menu).
params.backdrop: Color of the backdrop that dims the UI.
params.offset: Distance from the top when `align_y` is `"start"`.

pyzed.ui.modal.desc: A dialog. Use it as the `overlay` of `ui.layer`.

params.footer: Footer buttons, aligned to the right.
params.max_height: Scrolls content taller than this, keeping the header and footer in view.
params.on_close: The close button; also sent by Escape while the dialog has focus.

params.detail: Secondary text (for example, a file path).

pyzed.ui.command_palette.desc: A command palette: fuzzy-filters `commands` by `query` and shows their shortcuts.

params.on_query: Callable that receives the new text.

pyzed.ui.picker.desc: A searchable list on a floating surface. The basis of the palette and the file finder.

params.on_query: Callable that receives the new text.
params.empty_text: Text shown when there are no results.

pyzed.ui.fuzzy_match.desc: Returns `(score, positions)` if every letter of `query` appears in order in `candidate`; otherwise `None`. Rewards word starts and consecutive letters.

pyzed.ui.fuzzy_filter.desc: Filters and sorts `items` by fuzzy score. Returns `[(item, positions), ...]`.

params.key: Function that returns the text of each item.

pyzed.ui.highlighted.desc: Text with the characters at `positions` highlighted (fuzzy search matches).

params.progress: 0 to 1: a thin bar at the bottom (time left, a download).

pyzed.ui.toasts.desc: Shows `items` (usually `toast(...)`) stacked in the bottom-right corner over `base`.

pyzed.ui.popover.desc: Shows `content` (a `ui.menu`, a card…) over `base` at `(x, y)`. Clicking anywhere else calls `on_dismiss`. For a right-click menu, store the mouse position with `mouse_area(on_move=...)` and open the popover from `on_right_press` (see `examples/context_menu.py`).

pyzed.ui.editor.desc: A code editor: highlighting with the theme colors, line numbers and git markers.

params.id: Identifies the buffer (use the file path).
params.language: Language. If missing, it is inferred from `path`.
params.font: Typeface: `"mono"` by default; `"sans"` makes a multi-line text box, like a chat's message box.
params.annotations: `{line: "text"}` or `{line: ("text", color)}`: virtual text at the end of the line (code lens, diagnostics).
params.show_whitespace: Draws spaces as `·` and tabs as `→`.
params.tab_size: Tab inserts spaces up to the next multiple; Enter keeps the indentation (one more level after `:`); Backspace removes a level.
params.hard_tabs: With `tab_size`: Tab, Enter and indent (Ctrl+]) use tab characters instead of spaces.
params.backspace_unindent: With `tab_size`: Backspace in leading spaces removes a whole level (`False`: one space).
params.repeat_delay: Milliseconds Backspace and Delete wait, held down, before repeating (`None`: the system's).
params.repeat_rate: Deletions per second at most while Backspace or Delete is held down (`None`: the system's pace).
params.capture_keys: Keys the editor leaves to the app's `on_key` (`"up"`, `"enter"`…), e.g. while a completion list is open.
params.auto_close: Closes brackets and quotes as you type (and wraps the selection).
params.folding: Fold chevrons in the gutter; Ctrl+Shift+[ folds and Ctrl+Shift+] unfolds.
params.minimap: `True` (or a width in pixels) shows a minimap on the right.
params.cursor_color: Cursor color (the theme's player color by default).
params.on_zoom: Callable that receives `1`, `-1` or `0` for Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+wheel.
params.on_action: Callable that receives the name of each editor action that runs (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`…), e.g. to count them.
params.on_paste: Called after Ctrl+V (Cmd+V, Shift+Insert) pastes the clipboard's text, if it holds any: a chat box reads an image from the clipboard with `Command.paste_image`.
params.highlights: Ranges painted behind the text in the theme's search color: `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.
params.match_brackets: Outlines the bracket that matches the one next to the cursor (Ctrl+M jumps to it).
params.selection_highlight: Highlights the other occurrences of the selected text (Ctrl+D adds the next one as a cursor).
params.keymap: Zed-style `{binding: action}` dict (`{"ctrl-shift-d": "duplicate_line_down"}`); `None` as the action removes a default key. Build it from per-action overrides with `pyzed.ui.editor.keymap_for`.
params.readonly: `True` lets the text be selected and copied but not changed (a log, a traceback).
params.on_hover: Callable that receives `{line, column, start, end, x, y, height}` (the word under the mouse, from 1, and its place in the editor) after the mouse rests on it, and `None` when it leaves (hover cards).
params.hover_delay: Milliseconds the mouse rests on a word before `on_hover` is called.
params.sticky_scroll: How many lines of the enclosing blocks (`class`, `def`, `if`…) stay pinned at the top while scrolling (`0`: none).
params.indent_guides: `True` draws a thin line at each level of indentation (the one of the block around the cursor stands out); `"rainbow"` gives each depth its own color.

pyzed.ui.language_token.desc: Returns the highlighter language token for a path (`"main.rs"` → `"rs"`).

pyzed.ui.terminal.desc: A read-only terminal view with ANSI colors. It stays scrolled to the end.

params.lines: Text with ANSI escapes, or a list of lines of `(text, color)` segments.

pyzed.ui.ansi.desc: Converts text with ANSI colors into lines of `(text, color_name)` segments.

pyzed.ui.ColorPicker.desc: A component that picks a color with alpha, a linear gradient (stops you add, drag and remove, plus an angle) or a fill with an opacity mask. `on_change` gets a `"#rrggbb[aa]"` string, a `pz.Gradient` or a `pz.Paint`, all valid as a `background`. Pass the picked value back as `value`. See [Styles](/pyzed/theming/styles/#color-picker).

params.alpha: Shows the alpha bar and field.
params.swatches: Quick colors (default: the theme's accent and status colors).

pyzed.ui.color_swatch.desc: A small square showing a color, gradient or paint over a checkerboard.

pyzed.ui.checkerboard.desc: A light/dark checkerboard to draw under translucent colors.

pyzed.ui.Calendar.desc: A component with a month to pick a day on (`mode="single"`), a range (`"range"`: the first click starts it, the second ends it) or several days (`"multiple"`). The title opens a grid of months, then of years. Once clicked it takes the keyboard: arrows move, Enter picks, Page Up/Down change month. See the [Calendar](/pyzed/library/calendar/) page.

params.value: A date (`datetime.date` or `"2026-10-22"`), a `(start, end)` pair or a list of dates, by `mode`.
params.min: The earliest day that can be picked.
params.max: The latest day that can be picked.
params.disabled: Days that cannot be picked: dates, weekday names (`"sunday"`) or `"weekends"`.
params.week_numbers: Shows the ISO week number of each row.
params.show_outside: Shows the days of the months around.
params.on_change: Receives `event.value` (a date, a tuple or a list).

pyzed.ui.Calendar.example:
ui.Calendar(self.day, on_change=lambda e: setattr(self, "day", e.value))
ui.Calendar(self.stay, mode="range", months=2, on_change=lambda e: setattr(self, "stay", e.value))

pyzed.ui.DatePicker.desc: A component: a date field that opens a calendar below it, in a popup that panels never cut off. It can be typed in `format` (Enter or leaving the field reads it); once clicked, ↑/↓ move the date a day and Page Up/Down a month without opening anything, Alt+↓ opens the calendar and Escape closes it. See the [Date picker](/pyzed/library/date-picker/) page.

params.format: How it is written: `"DD/MM/YYYY"`, `"MMM D, YYYY"`... (see `format_date`).
params.disabled_dates: Days that cannot be picked (as in `Calendar`).
params.week_numbers: Shows week numbers in the calendar.
params.clearable: Shows an x that empties it.
params.today_button: Adds a Today link to the calendar.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.DatePicker.example: ui.DatePicker(self.due, format="DD/MM/YYYY", on_change=lambda e: setattr(self, "due", e.value))

pyzed.ui.DateRangePicker.desc: A component: a field for a start and an end date, with two months and quick ranges (Today, Last 7 days, This month...) in its popup. Typed text is two dates separated by `separator`. See the [Date range picker](/pyzed/library/date-range-picker/) page.

params.clearable: Shows an x that empties it.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.TimePicker.desc: A component: a time field with columns of hours and minutes (and seconds, and AM/PM with a 12-hour `format`) in a popup. Once clicked, ↑/↓ change it by `minute_step`. See the [Time picker](/pyzed/library/time-picker/) page.

params.clearable: Shows an x that empties it.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.TimePicker.example: ui.TimePicker(self.alarm, format="h:mm A", minute_step=15, on_change=lambda e: setattr(self, "alarm", e.value))

pyzed.ui.format_date.desc: Writes a date with a pattern of tokens: `YYYY` 2026, `YY` 26, `MMMM` October, `MMM` Oct, `MM` 10, `M` 10, `DD` 05, `D` 5, `dddd` Monday, `ddd` Mon, `HH`/`hh` hours, `mm` minutes, `ss` seconds, `A` AM/PM and `[text]` kept as is. A pattern with `%` is a `strftime` one. Month and day names follow the language of `pyzed.i18n`.

params.value: A date, a datetime, ISO text or `None` (gives `""`).
params.language: A language for the names instead of the current one.

pyzed.ui.parse_date.desc: Reads a date written with a pattern of `format_date` (month names in the current language or English); ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` always works. Returns `None` when the text is not a date.

pyzed.ui.format_time.desc: Writes a time (or `"14:30"`) with a pattern such as `"h:mm A"`.

pyzed.ui.parse_time.desc: Reads a time: `"14:30"`, `"2:30 PM"`, `"14:30:05"`, with `fmt` first. `None` when it is not one.

pyzed.ui.file_input.desc: A path field with a button that opens the system's file dialog, so nobody types a path by hand. See the [File picker](/pyzed/library/file-input/) page.

params.filters: Files shown: `{"Images": "png jpg"}` or `"Images: png, jpg"`.
params.title: The dialog's title.
params.directory: Where the dialog opens (default: the folder of the current path).
params.button: Text for the button instead of a folder icon.
params.editable: `False` keeps the path from being typed.
params.invalid: Paints the border in the error color.

pyzed.ui.system.pick.desc: The system's file dialog as a `Command`: return it from a callback and `then` receives what the user chose (a path, a list of paths with `"open_many"`, or `None` when they cancel). `ui.file_input` uses it.

params.title: The dialog's title.
params.filters: Files shown: `{"Images": "png jpg"}` or `"Images: png, jpg"`.

pyzed.ui.system.pick.example: ui.button("Open…", lambda: ui.system.pick(self.load, filters="Text: txt, md"))

pyzed.ui.DropZone.desc: A component that takes files dragged from the system's file manager and dropped on the window, and opens the file dialog on a click. It lights up while files are dragged over the window and keeps the dropped paths in `files`. The window's `on_file_drop` hook hands each file to the zone under the pointer, else to one whose `accept` lists its type. See the [Drop zone](/pyzed/library/drop-zone/) page.

params.text: The main text (default: Drop files here).
params.accept: Extensions (`["png", "jpg"]`), patterns (`"*.tar.gz"`) or `"folder"`; empty takes everything.
params.browse: A click opens the file dialog.
params.show_files: Lists the files under the text (each with an x).
params.live: `False` draws it without taking files (the designer's canvas).
params.on_drop: Receives `event.value`: one dropped path (once per file).
params.on_reject: Receives a path it does not accept.
params.on_enter: Files are dragged over the window.

pyzed.ui.ToolCall.desc: A component for one action of an AI agent, drawn like in Zed's Agent panel: a line with its icon, what it does and where (it unfolds to show the input and the output), or a card for edits and commands, with the diff or the output. While `status` is `"waiting"` it asks right on the card: Always allow, Allow or Reject. See [AI agents](/pyzed/editor/ai-agents/).

params.title: What it does ("Edit file").
params.detail: What it works on, in a monospace font.
params.images: PNG bytes shown under the output.
params.diffs: The edits it made: `{"path", "old", "new"}` dicts, shown as colored diffs (see `ui.diff_view`).
params.progress: What it printed so far (a command's output); its last lines show under the header while it runs.

pyzed.ui.ToolCall.example:
ui.ToolCall(title="Edit file", detail="ui/main.py", kind="edit", status=self.status,
            on_allow=lambda e: self.answer(True), on_deny=lambda e: self.answer(False))

pyzed.ui.Plan.desc: A component for an agent's plan: a checklist with `done/total` in its header, which folds it.

pyzed.ui.EditsBar.desc: A component listing the files an agent changed, like Zed's edits bar: `3 files changed` with Reject all and Keep all, unfolding to one row per file with its diff stat, Reject and Keep.

params.files: Dicts or objects with `path` and optional `added` and `removed` line counts.
params.on_keep_file: Keep on a file (`event.value` is its path).

pyzed.ui.ThreadHistory.desc: A component for past conversations: a search box and the threads grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, This week, This month, Older), each with a delete button.

params.threads: Dicts or objects with `id`, `title`, `updated` (a timestamp) and an optional `detail`.
params.selected: The id of the open thread.
params.on_open: A thread was picked (`event.value` is its id).
params.on_delete: Delete was pressed on a thread.

pyzed.ui.AuthPrompt.desc: A component that asks to sign in, like Zed when an agent needs it: one button per way to sign in, then, while one runs, what is happening (the browser or a terminal is open), a code to type when there is one, Open the page again and Cancel.

params.title: The heading.
params.methods: Dicts with `id`, `name`, optional `description` and `icon`; the first is the main one.
params.waiting: The id of the method in progress (`""` when none).
params.on_pick: A method was picked (`event.value` is its id).

pyzed.ui.AuthPrompt.example: ui.AuthPrompt(title="Sign in to Gemini", methods=[{"id": "google", "name": "Log in with Google"}], on_pick=self.sign_in)

pyzed.ui.ServiceRow.desc: A component for one thing an agent uses (an MCP server, an external agent, a skill), like the rows of Zed's agent settings: a status dot, the name and command, an on/off switch, a main button and a `⋯` menu.

params.name: Name.
params.detail: The command or URL, in a monospace font.
params.status_text: The dot's tooltip; shown under the name for errors and updates.
params.primary: Text of the main button (Update, Install…).

pyzed.ui.Catalog.desc: A component for things to install with a search box (agents from a registry, servers, skills…): each row shows Install, Installed or Update to a newer version.

params.items: Dicts or objects with `id`, `name` and optional `version`, `description`, `installed` and `update`.
params.on_install: Install or Update was pressed (`event.value` is the id).

pyzed.ui.context_meter.desc: How full a model's context window is, like Zed's token counter: a small ring and `48k / 200k`, yellow past 80% and red past 95%.

pyzed.ui.diff_view.desc: An edit as Zed shows it in a thread: the file's name, then the changed lines (green added, red removed) with a few lines around them.

params.diff: A dict with `path`, `old` and `new` (the texts before and after).
params.max_lines: Lines shown before `… N more lines`.
params.height: The most it grows to, in pixels; more lines scroll inside it (long lines scroll sideways).

pyzed.ui.led.desc: A round LED from Pyzed's brand: lit with a soft glow in the theme's `led` color (amber in the Pyzed themes) or dark in `led_off`.

params.color: Color token or hex instead of `led`.

pyzed.ui.led_toggle.desc: A toggle that shows its state with an LED next to a small mono label in capitals, like the SNAP and GUIDES switches of Pyzed Design's canvas.
pyzed.ui.led_toggle.example: ui.led_toggle("Snap", self.snap, lambda on: setattr(self, "snap", on))

pyzed.ui.lcd.desc: An LCD readout: the parts in amber mono on the theme's `display` color, split by dim bars (`None` and `""` are skipped).

params.color: Text color token or hex instead of `display_text`.

pyzed.ui.theme_rack.desc: Themes to pick from as a rack of modules: an LED lit on the current one, its name, eight swatches of its colors and a moon or a sun for dark and light. Pyzed Design's Settings use it.

params.on_pick: Called with the clicked theme's name.

pyzed.ui.theme_rack.example: ui.theme_rack(pz.themes.all(), self.theme.name, lambda name: setattr(self, "theme", name))

pyzed.ui.IconPicker.desc: A component that picks a Lucide icon: a search box (names and tags), a category drop-down and a grid that only builds the rows in view. Enter picks the first match. `on_change` gets the icon's name (`""` when cleared); pass it back as `value`. See the [Icon picker](/pyzed/library/icon-picker/) page.

params.clearable: Shows a button that clears the icon.
params.autofocus: Focuses the search box when it appears.

pyzed.ui.icon_picker_dialog.desc: A dialog with an `IconPicker` that picks on a click; use it as the dialog of `ui.dialog_layer`. The search box gets the focus.

params.on_pick: Called with the clicked icon's name (`""` when cleared).
params.title: Default: "Choose an icon", translated.
params.key: Component key, for several pickers in one view.

pyzed.ui.icon_picker_dialog.example:
ui.dialog_layer(page, ui.icon_picker_dialog(self.icon, self.pick, on_close=self.close) if self.picking else None,
                on_dismiss=self.close)

pyzed.ui.icon_grid.desc: The bare grid of icons, virtualized: only the rows in view are built, so thousands of icons cost the same as a few.

params.cell: Side of each cell in pixels.

pages.title: Themes
pages.description: API reference for pyzed Theme: the built-in themes, color tokens, deriving custom themes and color utilities for Python GUIs.
pages.intro: See the [theming](/pyzed/theming/themes/) guide for the list of tokens and how to create your own.

pyzed.Theme.desc: A theme: an immutable dataclass with color tokens (surfaces, borders, elements, text, status, editor, syntax, collaborator and ANSI colors) and metrics (`radius`, `radius_sm`, `ui_font_size`, `buffer_font_size`). The `is_dark` property tells whether it is dark.

pyzed.Theme.derive.desc: Returns a copy with some tokens changed. The `syntax` and `ansi` dicts are merged instead of replaced.

pyzed.Theme.color.desc: Resolves a token (`"accent"`, `"text_muted"`…) to its color. Hex colors and `"transparent"` pass through unchanged. Short names (`"muted"`, `"primary"`, `"danger"`…), Zed's names (`"text.muted"`) and the terminal colors (`"red"`…) work too; anything else raises `ValueError`.

pyzed.Theme.find_color.desc: Like `color`, but returns `None` for a name the theme does not know instead of raising.

pyzed.Theme.syntax_scopes.desc: Maps the theme's syntax tokens to TextMate scopes for the highlighter.

pyzed.Theme.palette.desc: The base palette passed to Iced for its internal styles. Internal use.

pyzed.Theme.with_accent.desc: A copy with a different accent color and everything that depends on it (focus, selection, links, primary buttons, text on accent).

pyzed.Theme.generate.desc: Creates a complete theme from a few colors. Surfaces, borders, hover states and muted text are mixed from `background` and `text`; the appearance is inferred from the background brightness if not given.

pyzed.Theme.from_zed.desc: Reads a theme from a Zed theme family file (`.json`) or a dict. A family usually has several (Ayu Dark/Light/Mirage); `name` picks one (the first by default).

params.name: Name of the theme within the family.

pyzed.Theme.to_dict.desc: A JSON-ready dict; `Theme.from_dict` reads it back.

pyzed.Theme.from_dict.desc: Creates a theme from `to_dict`. Missing tokens come from `base` (One Dark or One Light depending on `appearance`).

pyzed.Theme.save.desc: Saves the theme as JSON (Pyzed's own format).

pyzed.Theme.load.desc: Reads a theme written with `save` (for Zed themes use `from_zed`).

pyzed.themes.desc: Namespace with the built-in themes (Pyzed's own and the One, Ayu and Gruvbox families) and the theme registry. Built-in themes are also available as attributes: `themes.PYZED_DARK` (the default), `themes.PYZED_LIGHT`, `themes.ONE_DARK`, `themes.ONE_LIGHT`, `themes.AYU_DARK`, `themes.AYU_LIGHT`, `themes.AYU_MIRAGE`, `themes.GRUVBOX_DARK`, `themes.GRUVBOX_LIGHT`…

pyzed.themes.get.desc: Looks up a theme by name (case-insensitive). Raises `KeyError` if it doesn't exist.

pyzed.themes.register.desc: Adds (or replaces) a theme so it can be used by name.

pyzed.themes.load_zed.desc: Loads and registers every theme in a Zed family file.

pyzed.themes.auto.desc: A theme that follows the system's light/dark mode.

pyzed.AutoTheme.desc: What `themes.auto` returns: a `(light, dark)` pair. `pick(dark)` returns the right one.

pyzed.theme.current.desc: The theme components use when no `theme=` is passed.

pyzed.theme.use.desc: Changes the current theme. `App` does this before every `view()`, so you normally don't need it.

pyzed.theme.alpha.desc: Returns `color` with its opacity multiplied by `value`.

pyzed.theme.mix.desc: Mixes two colors: `amount=0` is `a` and `amount=1` is `b`.

pyzed.theme.resolve.desc: Turns an `App.theme` value (theme, name, `AutoTheme` or `None`) into a `Theme`.

params.dark: Whether the system is in dark mode.

pyzed.theme.luminance.desc: Relative luminance (WCAG) of a color, from 0 to 1.

pyzed.theme.contrast.desc: WCAG contrast ratio between two colors (1 to 21).

pyzed.theme.readable_on.desc: Returns `light` or `dark`, whichever has more contrast on `background`.

pyzed.brand.mark.desc: Pyzed's mark (the python that draws the “p”) as an SVG widget tinted with a theme color.

params.color: Color token or hex (`text_accent` by default).

pyzed.brand.wordmark.desc: The “pyzed” wordmark, with the python as its “p”; the dark version on dark themes.

pages.title: Icons
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.icons: the bundled Lucide icon set, icon names and file-type icon utilities for Python desktop interfaces.
pages.intro:
Pyzed bundles the [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) font (ISC license) with about 2000 icons.
Search names with `pyzed icons <filter>` or on the Lucide website.

pyzed.icons.icon.desc: An icon widget. Also available as `pyzed.icon`.

pyzed.icons.glyph.desc: Returns an icon's character, to use in any text with `font="icons"`. Raises `ValueError` if it doesn't exist.

pyzed.icons.names.desc: Sorted list of all icon names.

pyzed.icons.search.desc: Icons matching a search by name and tag, best first: exact names, then names that start with the query, names with every word and icons found by their tags (`search("person")` finds `user`).

params.query: Words that must all appear in the name or the tags.
params.among: Only search these names (default: every icon).

pyzed.icons.tags.desc: The search tags of an icon, from Lucide (`tags("user")` is `["person", "account", "contact"]`).

pyzed.icons.category.desc: The icons of a category of `CATEGORIES`, sorted. An icon can be in several.

pyzed.icons.CATEGORIES.desc: Groups for browsing icons (arrows, text, files, layout, media, communication, people, devices, development, shapes, weather, commerce, maps, status), each with the words of names and tags that put an icon in it.

pyzed.icons.for_file.desc: Returns `(icon, color_or_None)` for a file name, as in the project panel of a code editor.

pyzed.icons.language_for.desc: Human-readable language name of a file (`"main.py"` → `"Python"`), handy for the status bar.

pages.title: Drawing (pyzed.draw)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.draw: shapes, paths, text and transforms for drawing custom 2D graphics on a pz.canvas in Python desktop apps.
pages.intro:
`pyzed.draw` shapes are plain dicts you pass to [`pz.canvas`](/pyzed/reference/widgets/#canvas).
Angles are in degrees and `y` grows downwards. See the [drawing with canvas](/pyzed/guides/canvas/) guide.

```python
from pyzed import draw

pz.canvas([
    draw.background("#1e2127"),
    draw.circle(100, 100, 40, fill="#74ade8"),
    draw.text(100, 180, "Hello", color="#dce0e5", align_x="center"),
], width=200, height=200)
```

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.rects.desc: Many rectangles filled with one color in a single shape (fast for grids and bars).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.
`"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.polyline.desc: Joins `points` with straight lines (`closed=True` closes the shape).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.
`"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.arc.desc: A circular arc from `start` to `end` degrees (0 = 3 o'clock, clockwise). `pie=True` closes it through the center (pie slice).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.path.desc: A free-form path with SVG-like operations: `("M", x, y)` move, `("L", x, y)` line, `("Q", cx, cy, x, y)` quadratic curve, `("C", c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, x, y)` cubic curve, `("A", cx, cy, r, start, end)` arc, `("Z",)` close.

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.text.desc: Text anchored at `(x, y)`; `align_x`/`align_y` choose which side of the text sits on that point.

pyzed.draw.image.desc: A bitmap (sprite) drawn in the box `(x, y, w, h)`. Decoded once per source and cached, so drawing it every frame is cheap. See [Making games](/pyzed/games/).

params.source: A path, encoded image bytes (PNG, JPEG…) or raw RGBA bytes with `size`.

pyzed.draw.translate.desc: Offsets the shapes that come after it.

pyzed.draw.rotate.desc: Rotates the shapes that come after it around the current origin.

pyzed.draw.scale.desc: Scales the shapes that come after it.

pyzed.draw.save.desc: Saves the current transform (use it with `restore`).

pyzed.draw.restore.desc: Goes back to the transform saved by the last `save`.

pyzed.draw.group.desc: Draws `shapes` translated, rotated and scaled without affecting the following shapes. Returns a list: expand it with `*`.

pages.title: Visual designer (pyzed.designer)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.designer: run, open and build forms from Python code, and register toolbox components and templates.
pages.intro:
`pyzed.designer` is the code side of the [visual designer](/pyzed/editor/): run `.pzform` files,
open forms as windows, build forms in code, and extend the toolbox with your own components and
templates. [Designed components](/pyzed/editor/component-designer/) (`.pzcomp`) are loaded from here too.

```python
from pyzed import designer

designer.run("ui/main.pzform", reload=True)
```

pyzed.designer.binding.BIND_PROPS.desc: The property each control type binds, and whether the user edits it (two-way): `{type: (property, two_way)}`.

pyzed.designer.COMMON_EVENTS.desc: Events every control can handle in the designer's Events dock.

pages.title: Games (pyzed.game)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.game: held keys, movement, collisions, pixel sprites, particles and screen shake for real-time games on a pz.canvas.
pages.intro:
`pyzed.game` holds small helpers for real-time games: held keys, movement, collisions, pixel
sprites, particles and screen shake. They are plain Python built on [`pyzed.draw`](/pyzed/reference/draw/),
so they also work in screenshots and tests. See [Making games](/pyzed/games/) for complete examples.

```python
from pyzed import draw, game

def tick(self, dt):                      # pz.frames(self.tick) in subscriptions()
    self.x += game.axis(("left", "a"), ("right", "d")) * 300 * dt
    self.sparks.update(dt)

def view(self):
    return pz.canvas([draw.background("#0b0e14"), *game.glow(self.x, 200, 18, "#74ade8"),
                      *self.sparks.shapes()], width=400, height=300)
```

pyzed.game.pressed.desc: The keys held down right now, as a `frozenset` of names without modifiers (`"left"`, `"space"`, `"a"`…). Also available as `pz.pressed()`.

pyzed.game.is_pressed.desc: Whether any of `keys` is held down (`held` replaces `pressed()`, for tests). Also available as `pz.is_pressed()`.

pyzed.game.axis.desc: `-1`, `0` or `1` from two groups of keys: `axis(("left", "a"), ("right", "d"))`.

pyzed.game.vector.desc: A direction `(x, y)` of length 0 or 1 from four groups of keys (arrows and WASD by default); diagonals are normalized.

pyzed.game.lerp.desc: The value `t` of the way from `a` to `b` (`t` from 0 to 1).

pyzed.game.Rect.desc: An axis-aligned box (`x`, `y` is the top-left corner) with `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`, `center`, `overlaps(other)`, `contains(x, y)`, `moved(dx, dy)` and `shape(**paint)` (a `draw.rect`).

pyzed.game.circle_rect.desc: Where a circle hits a `Rect`: the push-out direction `(nx, ny)`, or `None`. A ball bounces with `if nx: vx = abs(vx) * nx` and `if ny: vy = abs(vy) * ny`.

pyzed.game.rgba.desc: `color` (`"#rrggbb[aa]"` or a tuple) as an `(r, g, b, a)` tuple with `alpha` applied.

pyzed.game.glow.desc: A soft light: translucent circles growing around `(x, y)` (bloom on a canvas). `strength` is the opacity of the innermost halo; `core=False` leaves out the solid circle.

pyzed.game.sprite.desc: Pixel art from text: each character of `rows` is a pixel colored by `palette` (missing characters are transparent). One shape per color, so a sprite stays cheap whatever its size.

pyzed.game.Particles.desc: Sparks, smoke, explosions: short-lived dots that move, fall and fade out. Call `burst(x, y, …)` when something happens, `update(dt)` every frame and draw `shapes()`; `gravity`, `drag` and `limit` tune them.

pyzed.game.Shake.desc: Screen shake: `kick(8)` on a hit, `update(dt)` every frame, and start the canvas shapes with `*shake.shapes()` (a translate) so everything moves together.

pages.title: Services (pyzed.services)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.services: timers, shortcuts, file watchers, processes, background workers, web requests, the clipboard, settings, file dialogs, notifications and tray icons for Python desktop apps.
pages.intro:
Services raise events but draw nothing: they are the non-visual components of Pyzed Design
([the tray under the form](/pyzed/editor/non-visual-components/)) and work the same in a
`pz.App` or a script. Handlers go in `on_<event>=`; events raised by a background thread reach
them on the app's thread. See the [Services guide](/pyzed/guides/services/).

```python
watcher = pz.FileWatcher("inbox", pattern="*.csv", on_created=self.import_file)
watcher.start()
```

pyzed.Timer.desc: Raises `tick` (with the count) every `interval` milliseconds while it is running; `repeat=False` ticks once. Return `subscriptions()` from your app's `subscriptions`.

pyzed.Shortcut.desc: Raises `activate` when one of its `keys` is pressed (`"ctrl-s"`, `"Ctrl+S"`, several separated by commas; `mod-` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere). Call `handle(combo)` from `on_key`.

pyzed.FileWatcher.desc: Watches a folder or a file and raises `created`, `modified` and `deleted` (a path) and `change` (the changed paths), checking every `interval` milliseconds. `start()`, `stop()`, `running`.

pyzed.Process.desc: Runs a program and raises `output` and `error_output` for every line it prints, `finished` with its exit code, `started` and `failed`. `start()`, `write()`, `kill()`, `wait()`.

pyzed.Worker.desc: Runs `work(value)` in a background thread with `run(value)`; `report()` raises `progress`, the result arrives in `done` and an exception in `failed`. `cancel()` sets `cancelled`.

pyzed.HttpRequest.desc: Calls a web address in the background: `send()` raises `response` with an `HttpResponse` (error statuses included) or `failed` when there was no answer. `json=` sends JSON.

pyzed.Clipboard.desc: The system clipboard: `copy(text)` and `paste()` return commands; with `watch=True` it raises `change` when something new is copied.

pyzed.Settings.desc: Values kept between runs: a dict saved as JSON in the user's settings folder at every change, with `defaults`; raises `change` with `(key, value)`.

pyzed.FileDialog.desc: The system's file dialog: `show()` returns the command that opens it in `mode` `"open"`, `"open_many"`, `"save"` or `"folder"`; raises `chosen` or `cancelled`.

pyzed.Notification.desc: A desktop notification: `show(text)` shows it and returns whether it could; raises `shown` or `failed`.

pyzed.TrayIcon.desc: An icon in the system tray with a `tooltip` and a `menu` (a list, or text with one item per line: `-` separator, `[x]` check, indented submenu): `show()` returns whether it could, `hide()`, `checked(item)`; raises `click`, `double_click` (Windows), `menu` and `failed`. On Linux it is a StatusNotifierItem, without GTK.

pyzed.TrayItem.desc: An entry of a `TrayIcon` menu: `text`, `id` (what `menu` receives), `enabled`, `checked` and `items` for a submenu.

pyzed.SystemInfo.desc: What the computer is: `os` (`"Windows"`, `"macOS"`, `"Linux"`), `os_version`, `machine`, `hostname`, `user`, `home`, `language`, `cpu_count`, `python_version`, `memory_total`, plus `memory_available`, `disk_free` and `disk_total` read when asked. `env(name)` reads a variable, `folder("documents")` finds the user's folders. With `interval` above 0, `start()` raises `update` with `snapshot()` every so often.

pyzed.Launcher.desc: Opens files, folders and links with the app the system uses for them: `open(target)`, `reveal(path)` (selected in the file manager) and `email(to, subject, body)`; raises `opened` or `failed`.

pyzed.NetworkMonitor.desc: Notices when the computer goes online or offline by reaching `host` every `interval` milliseconds in the background: `online`, `check()`, `start()`, `stop()`; raises `change`, `online` and `offline`.

pyzed.PowerMonitor.desc: The battery: `percent`, `plugged` and `has_battery`; every `interval` milliseconds raises `change`, `low` (under `low_level` while unplugged), `plugged` and `unplugged`.

pages.title: IoT and devices (pyzed.iot)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.iot: serial and USB serial ports, MQTT, WebSocket, UDP and TCP sockets, Modbus TCP and RTU, mDNS/SSDP network discovery and Bluetooth LE for Python desktop apps.
pages.intro:
Services that talk to devices: boards on a serial port, MQTT brokers, WebSockets, UDP and TCP
sockets, Modbus PLCs and meters, Bluetooth LE gadgets and what answers on the local network.
They work like the [services](/pyzed/reference/services/): handlers go in `on_<event>=`, the
connection runs in a thread of its own and events reach the handlers on the app's thread. In
Pyzed Design they are the components of the IoT category. See the
[IoT guide](/pyzed/guides/iot/).

```python
board = pz.SerialPort(match="arduino", baud_rate=115200, on_line=self.reading)
board.connect()

mqtt = pz.MqttClient("broker.local", subscribe="home/#", on_message=self.received)
mqtt.connect()
mqtt.publish("home/lamp/set", "on")
```

Every connection has `connect()`, `disconnect()`, `connected`, `running` and the events
`connected`, `disconnected` and `failed`; with `reconnect` (milliseconds) it comes back by itself.

pyzed.SerialPort.desc: A serial or USB serial port (Arduino, ESP32, Pico, GPS...): `port` names it (`"COM3"`, `"/dev/ttyUSB0"`) or, empty, the first one `match` names (`"arduino"`, `"2341:0043"`; empty: the first USB port). Raises `data` (bytes) and `line` (text); `write()`, `send_line()`, `reset()` (DTR), `set_baud_rate()`. `SerialPort.ports(match)` lists the ports. Opens the device again when it comes back (`reconnect`, 1000 ms by default).

pyzed.SerialWatcher.desc: Notices serial devices being plugged in and unplugged, every `interval` milliseconds: `plugged` and `unplugged` with a `PortInfo` (`name`, `kind`, `vid`, `pid`, `usb_id`, `manufacturer`, `product`, `description`), `change` with the list; `ports` is the last list.

pyzed.MqttClient.desc: An MQTT 3.1.1 client (Mosquitto, Home Assistant, EMQX...): `publish(topic, payload, qos, retain)`, `subscribe(topic)`, `unsubscribe()` and `on_topic(pattern, handler)` with the wildcards `+` and `#`. Each message raises `message` with an `MqttMessage` (`topic`, `payload`, `text`, `value`, `json()`); `last` keeps the last one of each topic. TLS, logins, QoS 0, 1 and 2, a last will, and the subscriptions kept after every reconnection (2000 ms by default).

pyzed.WebSocket.desc: A WebSocket client (`ws://`, `wss://`): `send()` text, bytes or JSON; each message raises `message` (text, bytes or, with `json=True`, the parsed data). `headers`, `protocols`, a ping every `ping_interval` milliseconds.

pyzed.UdpSocket.desc: Sends and receives UDP datagrams: `start()` listens on `port`, each one raises `message` with a `UdpMessage` (`data`, `text`, `json()`, `host`, `port`); `send(data, host, port)`, `reply(message, data)`, `broadcast` and `multicast_group`.

pyzed.TcpClient.desc: A TCP connection (optionally TLS) to a device or server: raises `data` and `line`; `write()` and `send_line()`.

pyzed.ModbusClient.desc: A Modbus client over TCP (`host`) or RTU (`serial_port`, RS-485): `read_coils`, `read_discrete_inputs`, `read_holding_registers`, `read_input_registers`, `read(table, address, format)` (`"float32"`, `"int32"`...), `write_coil`, `write_register`, `write_coils`, `write_registers` and `write(address, value, format)`. `poll` lines (`name table address [format] [count]`) are read every `interval` milliseconds and raise `update` with a dict. Raises `ModbusError` when the device refuses or does not answer.

pyzed.DeviceDiscovery.desc: Finds the devices of the local network with mDNS/Bonjour (`service`: `"_http._tcp"`, `"_esphomelib._tcp"`...; empty: all) and SSDP/UPnP: `scan()`, `start()`; raises `found` and `lost` with a `Device` (`name`, `host`, `port`, `address`, `kind`, `service`, `hostname`, `properties`, `url`), `change` and `done`. `pyzed.iot.resolve_local("esp32.local")` finds one address.

pyzed.BluetoothScanner.desc: Finds Bluetooth LE devices nearby for `timeout` milliseconds, filtered by `match` (name or address) and `services`: `scan()`, `start()`, `devices` (nearest first); raises `found` with a `BleDevice` (`address`, `name`, `rssi`, `uuids`, `manufacturer_data`), `change`, `done` and `failed`. Needs `pip install "pyzed-ui[bluetooth]"` (bleak).

pyzed.BluetoothDevice.desc: A connection to one Bluetooth LE device by `address` or `name`: `read(uuid)`, `write(uuid, data, response)`, `subscribe(uuid)`, `services()`; the characteristics in `notify` raise `notification` with a `BleNotification` (`uuid`, `data`, `text`, `value`). UUIDs can be short (`"2a37"`) or names (`"heart_rate_measurement"`, `"battery_level"`, `"nordic_uart_tx"`).

pages.title: Shader graphs (pyzed.shading)
pages.description: API reference for pyzed.shading: load .pzshad shader graphs, change their variables, and build node graphs in code that compile to the WGSL of pz.shader.
pages.intro:
`pyzed.shading` is the node-based shader system behind the designer's
[Shader view](/pyzed/shading/shader-designer/): `.pzshad` graphs of nodes that compile to the WGSL of
[`pz.shader`](/pyzed/reference/widgets/). See [Shader graphs](/pyzed/shading/shader-graphs/) for a tour.

```python
from pyzed import shading

fire = shading.load("shaders/fire.pzshad")
fire["speed"] = 2.0                       # a mutable variable: no recompiling
pz.shader(fire, width=320, height=200)    # or pz.shader("shaders/fire.pzshad")
```

pyzed.shading.load.desc: The `Shader` of a `.pzshad` file, cached by path (`fresh=True` reads it again). It reloads by itself when the file changes.

pyzed.shading.Shader.desc: A shader graph ready to draw, with its own values for the variables: `shader["speed"] = 2`, `shader.set(...)`, `shader.variables`, `shader.wgsl` and `shader.widget(...)`. `pz.shader` takes one directly.

pyzed.shading.widget.desc: A `pz.shader` widget for a `.pzshad` path, a `Graph` or a `Shader`.

pyzed.shading.Graph.desc: A shader graph: variables, nodes and the links between them. Call a node type on it to add one (`g.noise(scale=4)`, `g.sin(x)`), pick outputs with `node["name"]` and combine them with arithmetic. `save`, `compile`, `arrange`, `connect` and the variable methods edit it.

pyzed.shading.new.desc: A new graph with UV feeding a gradient into the Output node: the designer's Blank template.

pyzed.shading.load_graph.desc: The `Graph` of a `.pzshad` file, to edit it.

pyzed.shading.Variable.desc: A variable of a shader: `name`, `type` (float, int, bool, vec2, vec3, vec4, color, texture), `value`, `mutable` (a uniform) or constant, `min`, `max`, `step` and `description`.

pyzed.shading.Node.desc: A node of a graph: its `type`, position, `inputs` (fixed values of unconnected inputs), `params` (settings), `title` and whether its `preview` shows.

pyzed.shading.NodeRef.desc: What `Graph.add` returns: `ref["port"]` is an output to wire elsewhere; arithmetic uses its first output.

pyzed.shading.GraphError.desc: Raised for wires that can't connect (types, cycles), unknown node types and bad variable names.

pyzed.shading.compile.desc: Compiles a graph (or one node's output, for its preview) to WGSL: the `Compiled` code, uniforms, textures and problems by node.

pyzed.shading.Compiled.desc: The result of `compile`: `code`, `uniforms`, `textures`, `names` (the uniform of each variable), `errors` by node id, `uses_time`, and `check()`, which runs the GPU compiler and puts its messages on the node that wrote the line.

pyzed.shading.register.desc: Adds a node type of your own to the catalog (and the designer's Shading sidebar).

pyzed.shading.NodeType.desc: A node type: id, title, category, inputs, outputs, settings and how it writes its WGSL.

pyzed.shading.Preset.desc: An entry of the Shading sidebar: a node type with some settings (`func:sin` is the Function node set to sin).

common.content: Content: a `Widget`, a string or a number (converted to text).
common.children: List of children. Nested lists are flattened and `None` and `False` are ignored, so you can write `cond and widget`.
common.padding: Inner padding: `8`, `(vertical, horizontal)` or `(top, right, bottom, left)`.
common.align: Alignment of the children on the cross axis: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
common.clip: Clips content that overflows the bounds.
common.bg: Background color (`"#rrggbb[aa]"`, `(r, g, b[, a])` or `"transparent"`).
common.radius: Corner radius: a number or `(top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left)`.
common.on_press: Message or callable sent on press. `None` disables the control.
common.theme: Theme to use instead of the current one (`pyzed.theme.current()`).
common.id: Stable identifier used to focus or scroll it with a `Command`.
common.icon: Name of a Lucide icon (`pyzed icons` lists them).
common.icon_color: Icon color: a theme token or a hex color.
common.keys: Shortcut shown at the end, written as a string: `"ctrl-s"`, `"cmd-k cmd-s"`.
common.label: Label text.
common.title: Title.
common.on_dismiss: Message or callable sent on close.
common.actions: Extra widgets (usually buttons) shown as actions.
common.on_toggle: Callable that receives the new `bool` (or a message to send).
common.on_change: Callable that receives the new value.
common.on_select: Callable that receives the chosen item.
common.on_input: Callable that receives the new text on every keystroke.
common.on_submit: Message or callable sent when Enter is pressed.
common.on_close: Message or callable sent when the X is pressed.
common.app: An `App` instance (or the class, which is instantiated with no arguments).
common.mono: Uses the monospace font (IBM Plex Mono).
common.message: Any Python value, or a callable.
common.font: Font of the span or text (family name, e.g. `"IBM Plex Mono"`).
common.italic: If `True`, the span is drawn in italics.
common.wrap: Line wrapping / moves children to a new row when they don't fit.
common.on_move: Called with `(x, y)` when the mouse moves.
common.on_middle_release: Middle button released (pan gestures, for example).
common.active_line: Background color of the cursor line.
common.key: Key that identifies the subscription (defaults to the message or the function).
common.source: File path, `bytes` of the encoded file, or raw RGBA pixels with `size=(width, height)`.
common.on_menu: Message or callable for the menu button.
